sentences.zh: 李植，字汝培。

translations.literal: Li Zhi, style Rupei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi, styled Rupei.

sentences.zh: 父承式，自大同徙居江都，官福建布政使。

translations.literal: His father Chengshi moved from Datong to settle in Jiangdu and served as Fujian Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengshi had moved from Datong to Jiangdu and held the post of Fujian Provincial Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 植舉萬歷五年進士，選庶吉士，授御史。

translations.literal: Zhi passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Wanli, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Wanli reign, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, and was appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 十年冬，張居正卒，馮保猶用事。

translations.literal: In the winter of the tenth year, Zhang Juzheng died, but Feng Bao still held power.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the tenth year, Zhang Juzheng died, yet Feng Bao still wielded power at court.

sentences.zh: 其黨錦衣指揮同知徐爵居禁中，為閱章奏，擬詔旨如故。

translations.literal: His follower Xu Jue, an assistant commissioner of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, lived within the Forbidden City, reviewed memorials, and drafted edicts as before.
translations.idiomatic: His ally Xu Jue, an assistant commissioner of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, lived inside the palace, reviewed memorials, and drafted edicts just as before.

sentences.zh: 居正黨率倚爵以自結於保，爵勢益張。

translations.literal: Juzheng's faction generally relied on Jue to attach themselves to Bao, and Jue's power grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng's faction routinely used Jue to curry favor with Bao, and Jue's influence grew ever stronger.

sentences.zh: 而帝雅銜居正、保，未有以發。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor had long borne resentment against Juzheng and Bao and had no occasion to act.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long harbored resentment toward Juzheng and Bao, but had lacked an occasion to strike.

sentences.zh: 御史江東之首暴爵奸，並言兵部尚書梁夢龍與爵交歡，以得吏部，宜斥。

translations.literal: The censor Jiang Dongzhi was the first to expose Jue's wickedness, and also said that Minister of War Liang Menglong had been on intimate terms with Jue and thereby obtained the Ministry of Personnel, and ought to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The censor Jiang Dongzhi was the first to expose Jue's crimes, and charged that Minister of War Liang Menglong had won the Ministry of Personnel through his intimacy with Jue and ought to be removed.

sentences.zh: 帝下爵獄，論死，夢龍罷去。

translations.literal: The emperor imprisoned Jue and sentenced him to death; Menglong was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Jue thrown into prison and sentenced to death, and Menglong was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 植遂發保十二大罪。

translations.literal: Zhi then laid out Bao's twelve great crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi then enumerated twelve grave crimes committed by Bao.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，罪保。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and punished Bao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and punished Bao.

sentences.zh: 植、東之由是受知於帝。

translations.literal: Zhi and Dongzhi thereby won the emperor's favor.
translations.idiomatic: Through this, Zhi and Dongzhi won the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 明年，植巡按畿輔，請寬居正所定百官乘驛之禁，從之。

translations.literal: The next year Zhi toured as investigating censor in the capital region and requested that the restrictions Juzheng had imposed on officials' use of courier stations be relaxed; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, as investigating censor in the capital region, Zhi asked that the restrictions Juzheng had placed on officials' use of courier stations be eased, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 帝用禮部尚書徐學謨言，將卜壽宮於大峪山。

translations.literal: The emperor followed the advice of Minister of Rites Xu Xuemo and was about to choose a site for the mausoleum at Dayu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on the advice of Minister of Rites Xu Xuemo, the emperor planned to select a mausoleum site at Dayu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 植扈行閱視，謂其地未善。

translations.literal: Zhi accompanied the tour to inspect the site and said the ground was not good.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi accompanied the imperial tour to inspect the site and declared the location unsuitable.

sentences.zh: 欲偕東之疏爭，不果。

translations.literal: He wished to join Dongzhi in a memorial protest but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: He wished to join Dongzhi in a memorial of protest, but could not carry it through.

sentences.zh: 明年，植還朝。

translations.literal: The next year Zhi returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhi returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時御史羊可立亦以追論居正受帝知。

translations.literal: At that time the censor Yang Keli also won the emperor's favor by pursuing criticism of Juzheng.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the censor Yang Keli likewise won imperial favor by pressing the case against Juzheng.

sentences.zh: 三人更相結，亦頗引吳中行、趙用賢、沈思孝為重。

translations.literal: The three men drew closer to one another and also looked to Wu Zhongxing, Zhao Yongxian, and Shen Sixiao as men of weight.
translations.idiomatic: The three men banded together and also looked to Wu Zhongxing, Zhao Yongxian, and Shen Sixiao as allies of standing.

sentences.zh: 執政方忌中行、用賢，且心害植三人寵。

translations.literal: The chief ministers already resented Zhongxing and Yongxian, and in their hearts resented the favor shown the three men.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers already resented Zhongxing and Yongxian, and inwardly resented the favor the emperor showed Zhi and his two allies.

sentences.zh: 會爭御史丁此呂事及論學謨卜壽宮之非，與申時行等相拄，卒被斥去。

translations.literal: When the dispute over Censor Ding Cilü and criticism of Xuemo's choice of the mausoleum site collided with Shen Shixing and the others, they were ultimately driven out.
translations.idiomatic: When the dispute over Censor Ding Cilü and objections to Xuemo's mausoleum site brought them into conflict with Shen Shixing and his colleagues, all three were eventually driven from office.

sentences.zh: 初，兵部員外郎嵇應科、山西提學副使陸檄、河南參政戴光啟為鄉會試考官，私居正子嗣修、懋修、敬修。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ji Yingke, an assistant director in the Ministry of War, Lu Xi, vice commissioner for education in Shanxi, and Dai Guangqi, administrative commissioner in Henan, had served as examiners in the provincial and metropolitan examinations and had shown favoritism to Juzheng's sons Siziu, Maoxiu, and Jingxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Ji Yingke of the Ministry of War, Lu Xi, vice commissioner for education in Shanxi, and Dai Guangqi, administrative commissioner in Henan, had served as examiners in the provincial and metropolitan examinations and had favored Juzheng's sons Siziu, Maoxiu, and Jingxiu.

sentences.zh: 居正敗，此呂發其事。

translations.literal: After Juzheng's fall, Cilü exposed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: After Juzheng fell, Cilü exposed the affair.

sentences.zh: 又言：「禮部侍郎何雒文代嗣修、懋修撰殿試策，而侍郎高啟愚主南京試，至以『舜亦以命禹』為題，顯為勸進。」

translations.literal: He also said: Vice Minister of Rites He Luowen had written the palace examination essays for Siziu and Maoxiu, while Vice Minister Gao Qiyu had presided over the Nanjing examination and even set as its theme 'Shun likewise entrusted Yu,' plainly an effort to urge advancement.
translations.idiomatic: He further charged that Vice Minister of Rites He Luowen had written the palace examination essays for Siziu and Maoxiu, while Vice Minister Gao Qiyu had presided over the Nanjing examination and even set the theme 'Shun likewise entrusted Yu'—plainly a bid to urge Juzheng's sons forward.

sentences.zh: 大學士申時行、余有丁、許國皆嗣修等座主也，言考官止據文藝，安知姓名，不宜以此為罪，請敕吏部核官評，以定去留。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Shen Shixing, Yu Youding, and Xu Guo had all been chief examiners to Siziu and the others; they said examiners judge only on literary merit and cannot know candidates' names, that this ought not be made a crime, and asked that the Ministry of Personnel be ordered to review official evaluations to decide who should stay or go.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Shen Shixing, Yu Youding, and Xu Guo had all been chief examiners to Siziu and his brothers. They argued that examiners judge only literary merit and cannot know candidates' names, that such charges should not stand as crimes, and asked that the Ministry of Personnel review official evaluations to decide dismissals and retention.

sentences.zh: 尚書楊巍議黜雒文，改調應科、檄，留啟愚、光啟，而言此呂不顧經旨，陷啟愚大逆。

translations.literal: Minister Yang Wei proposed dismissing Luowen and transferring Yingke and Xi, while retaining Qiyu and Guangqi, and said Cilü had disregarded the classics and imputed treason to Qiyu.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yang Wei proposed dismissing Luowen and transferring Yingke and Xi while retaining Qiyu and Guangqi, and charged that Cilü had twisted the classics and falsely imputed treason to Qiyu.

sentences.zh: 此呂坐謫。

translations.literal: Cilü was punished by demotion.
translations.idiomatic: Cilü was demoted in consequence.

sentences.zh: 植、東之及同官楊四知、給事中王士性等不平，交章劾巍，語侵時行。

translations.literal: Zhi, Dongzhi, their colleague Yang Sizhi, the supervising secretary Wang Shixing, and others were indignant and submitted successive memorials impeaching Wei, with language that impinged on Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, Dongzhi, their colleague Yang Sizhi, the supervising secretary Wang Shixing, and others were outraged and submitted successive memorials impeaching Wei, with language that touched Shen Shixing as well.

sentences.zh: 東之疏言：「時行以二子皆登科，不樂此呂言科場事。

translations.literal: Dongzhi's memorial said: Shixing, whose two sons both passed the examinations, was displeased that Cilü spoke of examination affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Dongzhi wrote: 'Shixing, whose two sons both passed the examinations, was displeased that Cilü raised matters of the examination halls.

sentences.zh: 巍雖庇居正，實媚時行。」

translations.literal: Though Wei shielded Juzheng, he was in fact currying favor with Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Though Wei shielded Juzheng, he was in fact currying favor with Shixing.

sentences.zh: 時行、巍並求去。

translations.literal: Shixing and Wei both asked to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing and Wei both asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 帝欲慰留時行，召還此呂，以兩解之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to comfort Shixing and keep him, recalled Cilü, and sought to reconcile both sides.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to keep Shixing and comfort him, recalled Cilü, and sought to reconcile both sides.

sentences.zh: 有丁、國言不謫此呂，無以安時行、巍心。

translations.literal: Youding and Guo said that unless Cilü were demoted, Shixing's and Wei's minds could not be set at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Youding and Guo argued that unless Cilü were demoted, Shixing and Wei could not be reassured.

sentences.zh: 國反覆詆言者生事，指中行、用賢為黨。

translations.literal: Guo repeatedly vilified the memorialists as troublemakers and named Zhongxing and Yongxian as a faction.
translations.idiomatic: Guo repeatedly denounced the memorialists as troublemakers and branded Zhongxing and Yongxian a faction.

sentences.zh: 中行、用賢疏辨求去，語皆侵國，用賢語尤峻。

translations.literal: Zhongxing and Yongxian memorialized in defense and asked to leave office; their language impinged on Guo, and Yongxian's was especially sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxing and Yongxian memorialized in their own defense and asked to resign; both attacked Guo, and Yongxian's language was especially harsh.

sentences.zh: 國避位不出。

translations.literal: Guo withdrew from his post and would not appear.
translations.idiomatic: Guo withdrew from his post and refused to attend court.

sentences.zh: 於是左都御史趙錦，副都御史石星，尚書王遴、潘季馴、楊兆，侍郎沈鯉、陸光祖、舒化、何起鳴、褚鈇，大理卿溫純，及都給事中齊世臣、御史劉懷恕等，極論時行、國、巍不宜去。

translations.literal: Thereupon Left Censor-in-Chief Zhao Jin, Vice Censor-in-Chief Shi Xing, Ministers Wang Lin, Pan Jixun, and Yang Zhao, Vice Ministers Shen Li, Lu Guangzu, Shu Hua, He Qiming, and Chu Tie, Chief Judge of the Court of Judicial Review Wen Chun, and Chief Supervising Secretary Qi Shichen, Censor Liu Huaishu, and others argued at length that Shixing, Guo, and Wei ought not to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Zhao Jin, Left Censor-in-Chief, Shi Xing, Vice Censor-in-Chief, Ministers Wang Lin, Pan Jixun, and Yang Zhao, Vice Ministers Shen Li, Lu Guangzu, Shu Hua, He Qiming, and Chu Tie, Chief Judge Wen Chun of the Court of Judicial Review, Chief Supervising Secretary Qi Shichen, Censor Liu Huaishu, and others argued at length that Shixing, Guo, and Wei ought not to resign.

sentences.zh: 主事張正鵠、南京郎中汪應蛟、御史李廷彥、蔡時鼎、黃師顏等又力攻請留三臣者之失。

translations.literal: Section Director Zhang Zhenghu, Nanjing Bureau Director Wang Yingjiao, and Censors Li Tingyan, Cai Shiding, and Huang Shiyan again attacked forcefully the faults of those who had asked to retain the three ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Section Director Zhang Zhenghu, Nanjing Bureau Director Wang Yingjiao, and Censors Li Tingyan, Cai Shiding, and Huang Shiyan in turn attacked sharply the errors of those who had pleaded to keep the three ministers.

sentences.zh: 中行亦疏言：「律禁上言大臣德政。

translations.literal: Zhongxing also memorialized, saying: The law forbids memorializing on a great minister's virtue and achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxing also wrote: 'The law forbids memorializing on a great minister's virtue and achievements.

sentences.zh: 邇者襲請留居正遺風，輔臣辭位，群起奏留，贊德稱功，聯章累牘。

translations.literal: Of late, following the custom of begging to retain ministers left from Juzheng's day, when a chief minister resigned his post the whole body rose to memorialize that he stay, praising virtue and proclaiming merit in linked memorials piled high.
translations.idiomatic: Of late, following the custom left from Juzheng's day, whenever a chief minister offered to resign the whole body rose to beg him stay, praising his virtue and proclaiming his merit in memorial after memorial.

sentences.zh: 此諂諛之極，甚可恥也。

translations.literal: This is the height of flattery and is deeply shameful.
translations.idiomatic: This is flattery at its worst, and deeply shameful.

sentences.zh: 祖宗二百余年以來，無諫官論事為吏部劾罷者，則又壅蔽之漸，不可長也。」

translations.literal: In more than two hundred years since the founding of the dynasty, no remonstrating official discussing affairs of state has been impeached and dismissed by the Ministry of Personnel; this is again the beginning of obstruction and must not be allowed to grow.
translations.idiomatic: In more than two hundred years since the founding of the dynasty, no remonstrating official has been impeached and dismissed by the Ministry of Personnel for discussing affairs of state; this is again the beginning of obstruction and must not be allowed to grow.

sentences.zh: 帝竟留三臣，責言者如錦等指。

translations.literal: The emperor ultimately retained the three ministers and rebuked the memorialists as Jin and the others had indicated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ultimately kept the three ministers and rebuked the memorialists as Jin and his allies had urged.

sentences.zh: 其後，啟愚卒為南京給事中劉一相劾去，時行亦不能救也。

translations.literal: Afterward Qiyu was ultimately impeached and removed by Nanjing Supervising Secretary Liu Yixiang, and Shixing could not save him either.
translations.idiomatic: Later Qiyu was impeached and removed by Nanjing Supervising Secretary Liu Yixiang, and even Shixing could not save him.

sentences.zh: 帝追仇居正甚，以大臣陰相庇，獨植、東之、可立能發其奸，欲驟貴之，風示廷臣。

translations.literal: The emperor pursued his vendetta against Juzheng keenly; seeing that great ministers sheltered him in secret, he found that only Zhi, Dongzhi, and Keli could expose his wickedness, wished to raise them swiftly in rank, and signaled this to the court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pursued his vendetta against Juzheng with zeal. Seeing that great ministers still sheltered him in secret, he found that only Zhi, Dongzhi, and Keli could expose his crimes, wished to raise them swiftly in rank, and made this plain to the court.

sentences.zh: 一相又劾錦衣都督劉守有匿居正家資。

translations.literal: Yixiang also impeached Embroidered-Uniform Guard Commander Liu Shouyou for concealing Juzheng's family wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Yixiang also impeached Embroidered-Uniform Guard Commander Liu Shouyou for concealing Juzheng's family wealth.

sentences.zh: 帝乃諭內閣黜守有，超擢居正所抑丘橓、余懋學、趙世卿及植、東之凡五人。

translations.literal: The emperor then instructed the Grand Secretariat to dismiss Shouyou and to promote beyond the usual limits Qiu Zhen, Yu Maoxue, and Zhao Shiqing, whom Juzheng had suppressed, together with Zhi and Dongzhi—five men in all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered the Grand Secretariat to dismiss Shouyou and to promote beyond the usual limits Qiu Zhen, Yu Maoxue, and Zhao Shiqing, whom Juzheng had held back, together with Zhi and Dongzhi—five men in all.

sentences.zh: 時行等力為守有解，言橓等不宜驟遷。

translations.literal: Shixing and the others strove to exonerate Shouyou and said Zhen and the others ought not be promoted so abruptly.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing and his colleagues strove to exonerate Shouyou and argued that Zhen and the others ought not be promoted so abruptly.

sentences.zh: 帝重違大臣意，議雖寢，心猶欲用植等。

translations.literal: The emperor was loath to go against the great ministers' wishes; though the proposal was set aside, in his heart he still wished to employ Zhi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was reluctant to defy the great ministers; though the proposal was set aside, he still wished to employ Zhi and his allies.

sentences.zh: 頃之，植劾刑部尚書潘季馴朋黨奸逆，誣上欺君，季馴坐削籍。

translations.literal: Before long Zhi impeached Minister of Justice Pan Jixun for forming a faction of traitors, deceiving the sovereign and misleading the ruler; Jixun was punished by removal from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhi impeached Minister of Justice Pan Jixun for forming a treacherous faction and deceiving the throne; Jixun was struck from the registers.

sentences.zh: 帝遂手詔吏部擢植太仆少卿，東之光祿少卿，可立尚寶少卿，並添註。

translations.literal: The emperor then personally instructed the Ministry of Personnel to promote Zhi to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, Dongzhi to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Keli to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Seals, all with additional appointments.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then personally ordered the Ministry of Personnel to promote Zhi to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, Dongzhi to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Keli to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Seals, each with an additional appointment.

sentences.zh: 廷臣益忌植等。

translations.literal: Court officials resented Zhi and the others all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials resented Zhi and his allies all the more.

sentences.zh: 十三年四月旱，御史蔡系周言：「古者，朝有權臣，獄有冤囚，則旱。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirteenth year there was drought; Censor Cai Xizhou said: In antiquity, when the court had powerful ministers or the prisons held wrongfully convicted men, there was drought.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the thirteenth year there was drought. Censor Cai Xizhou wrote: 'In antiquity, when the court harbored powerful ministers or the prisons held the wrongly convicted, drought followed.

sentences.zh: 植數為人言：『至尊呼我為兒，每觀沒入寶玩則喜我。』

translations.literal: Zhi has often told others: The sovereign calls me his son, and whenever he views the confiscated treasures he is pleased with me.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi has often boasted: "The sovereign calls me his son, and whenever he views the confiscated treasures he is pleased with me.

sentences.zh: 其無忌憚如此。

translations.literal: His lack of restraint is such as this.
translations.idiomatic: His lack of restraint is such as this.

sentences.zh: 陛下欲雪枉，而刑部尚書之枉，先不得雪。

translations.literal: Your Majesty wishes to redress wrongs, yet the wrong done to the Minister of Justice has not first been redressed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty wishes to redress wrongs, yet the wrong done to the Minister of Justice has not first been redressed.

sentences.zh: 今日之旱，實由於植。」

translations.literal: Today's drought is in truth owing to Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Today's drought is in truth owing to Zhi.'

sentences.zh: 又曰：「植迫欲得中行柄國，以善其後；

translations.literal: He also said: Zhi is urgently trying to have Zhongxing wield state power so as to secure his own future.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: 'Zhi is urgently trying to have Zhongxing wield state power so as to secure his own future;

sentences.zh: 中行迫欲得植秉銓，而騁其私。

translations.literal: Zhongxing is urgently trying to have Zhi hold the power of appointment so as to pursue his private ends.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxing is urgently trying to have Zhi hold the power of appointment so as to pursue his private ends.

sentences.zh: 倘其計得行，勢必盡毒善類，今日旱災猶其小者。」

translations.literal: If their scheme succeeds, they will surely destroy all good men; today's drought disaster would be the lesser of the evils.
translations.idiomatic: If their scheme succeeds, they will surely destroy all good men; today's drought would be the lesser of the evils.

sentences.zh: 其他語絕狂誕。

translations.literal: His other language was utterly wild and absurd.
translations.idiomatic: His other language was utterly wild and absurd.

sentences.zh: 所稱尚書，謂季馴也。

translations.literal: The minister he referred to was Jixun.
translations.idiomatic: The minister he referred to was Jixun.

sentences.zh: 疏上，未報，御史龔懋賢、孫愈賢繼之。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but received no reply; Censors Gong Maoxian and Sun Yuxian followed with their own.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but received no reply; Censors Gong Maoxian and Sun Yuxian followed with memorials of their own.

sentences.zh: 東之發憤上疏曰：「思孝、中行、用賢及張嶽、鄒元標數臣，忠義天植，之死不移，臣實安為之黨，樂從之遊。

translations.literal: Dongzhi, in indignation, memorialized: Sixiao, Zhongxing, Yongxian, Zhang Yue, Zou Yuanbiao, and several other ministers were loyal and righteous by nature and unshaken unto death; how could I be their faction? I am glad to keep company with them.
translations.idiomatic: Dongzhi, in indignation, memorialized: 'Sixiao, Zhongxing, Yongxian, Zhang Yue, Zou Yuanbiao, and several other ministers were loyal and righteous by nature and unshaken unto death. How could I be their faction? I am glad to keep company with them.

sentences.zh: 今指植與交歡為黨，則植猶未若臣之密，願先罷臣官。」

translations.literal: Now if pointing to Zhi's intimacy as a faction, then Zhi is not yet as close to me as that; I ask that my office be dismissed first.
translations.idiomatic: Now if Zhi's intimacy is called a faction, then Zhi is not yet as close to me as that; I ask that my office be dismissed first.

sentences.zh: 不允。

translations.literal: This was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: This was not granted.

sentences.zh: 可立亦抗言：「奸黨懷馮、張私惠，造不根之辭，以傾建言諸臣，勢不盡去臣等不止。」

translations.literal: Keli also protested: The wicked faction, cherishing private favors from Feng and Zhang, fabricates groundless charges to overthrow the memorializing ministers; they will not stop until we are all removed.
translations.idiomatic: Keli also protested: 'The wicked faction, cherishing private favors from Feng and Zhang, fabricates groundless charges to overthrow the memorializing ministers; they will not stop until we are all removed.'

sentences.zh: 乞罷職。

translations.literal: He begged to resign his post.
translations.idiomatic: He begged to resign his post.

sentences.zh: 章下內閣，時行等請詰可立奸黨主名。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the Grand Secretariat; Shixing and the others asked that Keli be required to name the leaders of the wicked faction.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was sent to the Grand Secretariat; Shixing and his colleagues asked that Keli be required to name the leaders of the wicked faction.

sentences.zh: 帝仍欲兩為之解，寢閣臣奏，而敕都察院：「自今諫官言事，當顧國家大體，毋以私滅公，犯者必罪。」

translations.literal: The emperor still wished to reconcile both sides, set aside the Grand Secretaries' memorial, and instructed the Censorate: From now on remonstrating officials discussing affairs must consider the great interest of the state, must not let private ends destroy the public good, and offenders will certainly be punished.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still wished to reconcile both sides, set aside the Grand Secretaries' memorial, and instructed the Censorate: 'From now on, when remonstrating officials discuss affairs of state, they must consider the greater interest of the realm, must not let private ends destroy the public good, and offenders will certainly be punished.'

sentences.zh: 植、東之求去，不許。

translations.literal: Zhi and Dongzhi asked to leave office but were not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and Dongzhi asked to resign but were not permitted.

sentences.zh: 給事御史齊世臣、吳定等交章劾可立不當代植辨。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries and censors Qi Shichen, Wu Ding, and others submitted successive memorials impeaching Keli for improperly speaking on Zhi's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries and censors Qi Shichen, Wu Ding, and others submitted successive memorials impeaching Keli for improperly speaking on Zhi's behalf.

sentences.zh: 報曰：「朕方憂旱，諸臣何紛爭？」

translations.literal: The reply said: I am now troubled by drought—why are the ministers quarreling?
translations.idiomatic: The reply said: 'I am now troubled by drought—why are the ministers quarreling?'

sentences.zh: 乃已。

translations.literal: And thereupon the matter ceased.
translations.idiomatic: And thereupon the matter ceased.

sentences.zh: 七月，御史龔仲慶又劾植、中行、思孝為邪臣，帝惡其排擠，出之外。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Censor Gong Zhongqing again impeached Zhi, Zhongxing, and Sixiao as wicked ministers; the emperor, disgusted by the factional strife, sent them out of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Censor Gong Zhongqing again impeached Zhi, Zhongxing, and Sixiao as wicked ministers; the emperor, disgusted by the factional strife, sent them out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 世臣及御史顧鈐等連章論救，不聽。

translations.literal: Shichen and Censor Gu Qian and others submitted successive memorials pleading for them, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Shichen and Censor Gu Qian and others submitted successive memorials pleading for them, but the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 是時，竟用學謨言，作壽宮於大峪山。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor ultimately followed Xuemo's advice and built the mausoleum at Dayu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the emperor ultimately followed Xuemo's advice and built the mausoleum at Dayu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 八月，役既興矣，大學士王錫爵，植館師，東之、可立又嘗特薦之於朝，錫爵故以面折張居正，為時所重。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, once the labor had begun, Grand Secretary Wang Xijue—Zhi's tutor in the academy, and whom Dongzhi and Keli had also specially recommended at court—was respected in his time for having openly rebuked Zhang Juzheng to his face.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, once construction had begun, Grand Secretary Wang Xijue—Zhi's tutor in the academy, and whom Dongzhi and Keli had also specially recommended at court—was respected in his time for having openly rebuked Zhang Juzheng to his face.

sentences.zh: 三人念時行去，錫爵必為首輔，而壽宮地有石，時行以學謨故主之，可用是罪也，乃合疏上言：「地果吉則不宜有石，有石則宜奏請改圖。

translations.literal: The three men reflected that when Shixing left, Xijue would surely become chief grand secretary, and that since the mausoleum site had stone and Shixing had backed the plan because of Xuemo, they could use this as a charge; they therefore submitted a joint memorial saying: If the ground is truly auspicious it ought not have stone; if it has stone one ought to memorialize and request a change of plan.
translations.idiomatic: The three men reasoned that when Shixing left, Xijue would surely become chief grand secretary, and that since the mausoleum site contained stone and Shixing had backed the plan because of Xuemo, they could use this as a charge. They therefore submitted a joint memorial: 'If the ground is truly auspicious it ought not contain stone; if it contains stone one ought to memorialize and request a change of plan.

sentences.zh: 乃學謨以私意主其議，時行以親故贊其成。

translations.literal: Yet Xuemo had led the discussion from private motive, and Shixing had aided its completion because of personal ties.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Xuemo had led the discussion from private motive, and Shixing had aided its completion because of personal ties.

sentences.zh: 今鑿石以安壽宮者，與曩所立表，其地不一。

translations.literal: Now in carving away stone to place the mausoleum, the ground is not the same as the marker set up before.
translations.idiomatic: Now in carving away stone to place the mausoleum, the ground is not the same as the marker set up before.

sentences.zh: 朦朧易徙，若弈棋然，非大臣謀國之忠也。」

translations.literal: Shifting the site obscurely as if moving pieces on a chessboard—this is not the loyalty with which great ministers plan for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Shifting the site obscurely as if moving pieces on a chessboard—this is not the loyalty with which great ministers plan for the state.

sentences.zh: 時行奏辨，言：「車駕初閱時，植、東之見臣直廬，力言形龍山不如大峪。

translations.literal: Shixing memorialized in defense, saying: When the imperial carriage first inspected the site, Zhi and Dongzhi came to my lodge in the palace and strongly argued that Xinglong Mountain was inferior to Dayu.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing memorialized in defense: 'When the imperial carriage first inspected the site, Zhi and Dongzhi came to my lodge in the palace and strongly argued that Xinglong Mountain was inferior to Dayu.

sentences.zh: 今已二年，忽創此議。

translations.literal: Now two years have passed and they suddenly raise this objection.
translations.idiomatic: Now two years have passed and they suddenly raise this objection.

sentences.zh: 其借事傾臣明甚。」

translations.literal: Their using the affair to overthrow me is very clear.
translations.idiomatic: Their using the affair to overthrow me is very clear.

sentences.zh: 帝責三人不宜以葬師術責輔臣，奪俸半歲。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked the three men for improperly using geomantic arts to charge the chief minister and docked their salaries for half a year.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked the three men for improperly using geomantic arts to charge the chief minister and docked their salaries for half a year.

sentences.zh: 三人以明習葬法薦侍郎張嶽、太常何源。

translations.literal: The three men, claiming expertise in burial practice, recommended Vice Minister Zhang Yue and Court of Imperial Sacrifices Director He Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: The three men, claiming expertise in burial practice, recommended Vice Minister Zhang Yue and Court of Imperial Sacrifices Director He Yuan.

sentences.zh: 兩人方疏辭，錫爵忽奏言恥為植三人所引，義不可留，因具奏不平者八事。

translations.literal: The two men had just memorialized to decline, when Xijue suddenly memorialized that he was ashamed to be cited by Zhi and the other three, that by right he could not remain, and set forth eight grievances in full.
translations.idiomatic: The two men had just memorialized to decline, when Xijue suddenly wrote that he was ashamed to be cited by Zhi and the other three, that by right he could not remain, and set forth eight grievances in full.

sentences.zh: 大略言：「張、馮之獄，上誌先定，言者適投其會，而輒自附於用賢等攖鱗折檻之黨。

translations.literal: In general he said: In the cases of Zhang and Feng, the sovereign's mind was already set; the memorialists merely happened to strike the moment, yet they at once attached themselves to the faction of Yongxian and others who had grasped the dragon's scales and broken the balustrade.
translations.idiomatic: In general he wrote: 'In the cases of Zhang and Feng, the sovereign's mind was already set; the memorialists merely happened to strike the moment, yet they at once attached themselves to the faction of Yongxian and others who had grasped the dragon's scales and broken the balustrade.

sentences.zh: 且謂舍建言別無人品；

translations.literal: Moreover they held that apart from memorializing there was no other measure of character.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover they held that apart from memorializing there was no other measure of character;

sentences.zh: 建言之中，舍采摭張、馮舊事，別無同誌。

translations.literal: Among memorializers, apart from gathering and collecting old stories about Zhang and Feng, there was no other bond of purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Among the memorializers, apart from recycling old stories about Zhang and Feng, they shared no other bond of purpose.

sentences.zh: 以中人之資，乘一言之會，超越朝右，日尋戈矛。

translations.literal: With mediocre talent, seizing the chance of a single remark, they surpassed those to their right at court and daily sought weapons of strife.
translations.idiomatic: With only mediocre talent, they seized the chance of a single remark, rose above their seniors at court, and daily provoked strife.

sentences.zh: 大臣如國、巍、化輩，曩嘗舉為正人。

translations.literal: Great ministers such as Guo, Wei, and Hua had once been raised up as upright men.
translations.idiomatic: Great ministers such as Guo, Wei, and Hua had once been acclaimed as upright men.

sentences.zh: 一言相左，日謀事刂刃，皆不平之大者。」

translations.literal: One word in disagreement, and daily they plotted to sharpen blades against them—all grave grievances.
translations.idiomatic: At the slightest disagreement they daily plotted against them with drawn blades—all grave grievances.

sentences.zh: 御史韓國楨，給事中陳與郊、王敬民等因叠攻植等，帝下敬民疏，貶植戶部員外郎，東之兵部員外郎，可立大理評事。

translations.literal: Censor Han Guozhen, Supervising Secretaries Chen Yujiao and Wang Jingmin, and others piled attacks on Zhi and his allies; the emperor issued Jingmin's memorial and demoted Zhi to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, Dongzhi to Vice Director in the Ministry of War, and Keli to Reviewing Officer in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Han Guozhen, Supervising Secretaries Chen Yujiao and Wang Jingmin, and others piled attacks on Zhi and his allies. The emperor issued Jingmin's memorial and demoted Zhi to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, Dongzhi to Vice Director in the Ministry of War, and Keli to Reviewing Officer in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 張嶽以諸臣紛爭，具疏評其賢否，頗為植、東之、可立地，請令各宣力一方，以全終始。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue, because the ministers were quarreling, submitted a full memorial evaluating their worth, spoke rather on behalf of Zhi, Dongzhi, and Keli, and asked that each be sent to serve his talents in one region so as to preserve their course from start to finish.
translations.idiomatic: Because the ministers were quarreling, Zhang Yue submitted a full memorial evaluating their worth, spoke rather on behalf of Zhi, Dongzhi, and Keli, and asked that each be sent to serve in one region so as to preserve his course from start to finish.

sentences.zh: 於時行、國、錫爵、巍、化、光祖、世臣、定、愈賢皆褒中寓刺，而力詆季馴、懋賢、系周、仲慶，惟中行、用賢、思孝無所譏貶。

translations.literal: Of Shixing, Guo, Xijue, Wei, Hua, Guangzu, Shichen, Ding, and Yuxian he spoke praise with hidden barbs, while fiercely denouncing Jixun, Maoxian, Xizhou, and Zhongqing; only Zhongxing, Yongxian, and Sixiao received no blame.
translations.idiomatic: Of Shixing, Guo, Xijue, Wei, Hua, Guangzu, Shichen, Ding, and Yuxian he offered praise laced with barbs, while fiercely denouncing Jixun, Maoxian, Xizhou, and Zhongqing; only Zhongxing, Yongxian, and Sixiao escaped censure.

sentences.zh: 帝責嶽頌美大臣，且支蔓，不足定國是，嶽坐免。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Yue for praising great ministers, and said the memorial was rambling and insufficient to settle the affairs of state; Yue was dismissed in consequence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Yue for praising great ministers and said the memorial was rambling and insufficient to settle the affairs of state; Yue was dismissed in consequence.

sentences.zh: 帝猶以植言壽宮有石數十丈，如屏風，其下皆石，恐寶座將置於石上。

translations.literal: The emperor still believed Zhi's statement that the mausoleum had a stone screen dozens of feet high, with stone below, fearing the imperial seat would be placed upon stone.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still believed Zhi's claim that the mausoleum had a stone screen dozens of feet high, with stone beneath, and feared the imperial seat would rest upon stone.

sentences.zh: 閏月，復躬往視之，終謂大峪吉，遂調三人於外。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month he again went in person to inspect it, still judged Dayu auspicious, and transferred the three men outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month he again went in person to inspect the site, still judged Dayu auspicious, and transferred the three men out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 御史柯梃因自言習葬法，力稱大峪之美，獲督南畿學政。

translations.literal: Censor Ke Ting, claiming expertise in burial practice, strongly praised the excellence of Dayu and was appointed to supervise education in the southern capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Ke Ting, claiming expertise in burial practice, strongly praised Dayu's excellence and was appointed to supervise education in the southern capital region.

sentences.zh: 而植同年生給事中盧逵亦承風請正三人罪，士論哂之。

translations.literal: Zhi's fellow jinshi Supervising Secretary Lu Kui likewise followed the trend and asked that the three men's crimes be set right; public opinion sneered at him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's fellow jinshi Supervising Secretary Lu Kui likewise followed the trend and asked that the three men's crimes be corrected; public opinion sneered at him.

sentences.zh: 植、東之、可立自以言事見知，未及三歲而貶。

translations.literal: Zhi, Dongzhi, and Keli, who had thought themselves known for memorializing, were demoted before three years had passed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, Dongzhi, and Keli, who had thought themselves known for memorializing, were demoted before three years had passed.

sentences.zh: 植得綏德知州，旋引疾歸。

translations.literal: Zhi received the post of prefect of Suide and soon returned home citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was appointed prefect of Suide and soon returned home citing illness.

sentences.zh: 居十年，起沅州知州。

translations.literal: After ten years at home he was recalled as prefect of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years at home he was recalled as prefect of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 屢官右僉都御史，巡撫遼東。

translations.literal: He rose repeatedly to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and served as grand coordinator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and served as grand coordinator of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 時二十六年也。

translations.literal: This was in the twenty-sixth year.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the twenty-sixth year.

sentences.zh: 植墾土積粟，得田四萬畝，歲獲糧萬石。

translations.literal: Zhi opened land and accumulated grain, obtaining forty thousand mu of fields and ten thousand shi of grain each year.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi opened land and stockpiled grain, reclaiming forty thousand mu of fields and harvesting ten thousand shi of grain each year.

sentences.zh: 戶部推其法九邊。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue promoted his method to the nine border regions.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue promoted his method to the nine border regions.

sentences.zh: 以倭寇退，請因師旋，選主、客銳卒，驅除宿寇，恢復舊遼陽。

translations.literal: When the Japanese pirates withdrew, he asked that as the army returned, crack troops of home and guest forces be selected to drive out entrenched bandits and recover old Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Japanese pirates withdrew, he asked that as the army returned home, crack troops be selected to drive out entrenched bandits and recover old Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 詔下總督諸臣詳議，不果行。

translations.literal: An edict was issued for the grand coordinators to discuss in detail, but it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued for the grand coordinators to discuss the plan in detail, but it was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 奏稅監高淮貪暴，請召還，不報。

translations.literal: He memorialized on the greed and violence of mining tax supervisor Gao Huai and asked that he be recalled; no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on the greed and violence of mining tax supervisor Gao Huai and asked that he be recalled; no reply came.

sentences.zh: 後淮激變，委阻撓罪於植。

translations.literal: Later when Huai stirred up trouble, he shifted blame for obstruction onto Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Huai stirred up trouble, he shifted blame for obstruction onto Zhi.

sentences.zh: 植疏辨乞休，帝慰留之。

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized in defense and asked to retire; the emperor comforted him and kept him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi memorialized in his own defense and asked to retire; the emperor comforted him and kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 明年，錦、義失事，巡按御史王業弘劾植及諸將失律。

translations.literal: The next year when Jin and Yi met disaster, Investigating Censor Wang Yehong impeached Zhi and the generals for breach of discipline.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when Jin and Yi suffered defeat, Investigating Censor Wang Yehong impeached Zhi and the generals for breach of discipline.

sentences.zh: 植以卻敵聞，且詆業弘。

translations.literal: Zhi was known for repelling the enemy and also vilified Yehong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi was known for repelling the enemy and also vilified Yehong.

sentences.zh: 業弘再疏劾植欺蔽，詔解官聽勘。

translations.literal: Yehong again memorialized impeaching Zhi for deception; an edict removed him from office pending investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Yehong again memorialized impeaching Zhi for deception; an edict removed him from office pending investigation.

sentences.zh: 勘已，命家居聽用，竟不召。

translations.literal: After the investigation he was ordered to remain at home awaiting employment, but was never summoned.
translations.idiomatic: After the investigation he was ordered to remain at home awaiting employment, but was never summoned.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: At death he was posthumously granted Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously granted Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 可立，汝陽人。

translations.literal: Keli was a native of Ruyang.
translations.idiomatic: Keli was a native of Ruyang.

sentences.zh: 由安邑知縣為御史，與植等並擢。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Anyi he became censor and was promoted together with Zhi and the others.
translations.idiomatic: From magistrate of Anyi he became censor and was promoted together with Zhi and the others.

sentences.zh: 已，由評事調大名推官。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred from reviewing officer to push officer of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred from reviewing officer to push officer of Daming.

sentences.zh: 終山東僉事。

translations.literal: He ended as Surveillance Commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Surveillance Commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 江東之，字長信，歙人。

translations.literal: Jiang Dongzhi, style Changxin, was a native of She county.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Dongzhi, styled Changxin, came from She county.

sentences.zh: 萬歷五年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 由行人擢御史。

translations.literal: From Court of State Ceremonial messenger he was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: From a post as messenger in the Court of State Ceremonial he was promoted to censor.

sentences.zh: 首發馮保、徐爵奸，受知於帝。

translations.literal: He was first to expose Feng Bao and Xu Jue's wickedness and won the emperor's favor.
translations.idiomatic: He was the first to expose the crimes of Feng Bao and Xu Jue and won the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 僉都御史王宗載嘗承張居正指，與於應昌共陷劉臺，東之疏劾之。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Zongzai had once carried out Zhang Juzheng's orders and together with Yu Yingchang had framed Liu Tai; Dongzhi memorialized to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Zongzai had once carried out Zhang Juzheng's orders and, together with Yu Yingchang, had framed Liu Tai; Dongzhi memorialized to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 故事，御史上封事，必以副封白長官。

translations.literal: By precedent, when a censor submitted a sealed memorial he had to inform the chief official with a copy.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when a censor submitted a sealed memorial he had to inform the chief official with a copy.

sentences.zh: 東之持入署，宗載迎謂曰：「江御史何言？」

translations.literal: Dongzhi brought it into the office; Zongzai greeted him asking, "What does Censor Jiang say?
translations.idiomatic: Dongzhi brought it into the office. Zongzai greeted him and asked, "What does Censor Jiang say?

sentences.zh: 曰：「為死御史鳴冤。」

translations.literal: He said, "I speak for a dead censor to right a wrong."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I speak for a dead censor to right a wrong."

sentences.zh: 問為誰？

translations.literal: Asked for whom?
translations.idiomatic: Asked for whom?

sentences.zh: 曰：「劉臺也。」

translations.literal: He said, "Liu Tai.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Liu Tai.

sentences.zh: 宗載失氣反走，遂與應昌俱得罪。

translations.literal: Zongzai lost his breath and ran back; he and Yingchang were both punished.
translations.idiomatic: Zongzai turned pale and fled; he and Yingchang were both punished.

sentences.zh: 東之出視畿輔屯政，奏駙馬都尉侯拱宸從父豪奪民田，置於理。

translations.literal: Dongzhi went out to inspect military colonies in the capital region and memorialized that Marquis Hou Gongchen, the emperor's son-in-law, had had his father violently seize commoners' fields and placed the matter in the hands of the law.
translations.idiomatic: Dongzhi went out to inspect military colonies in the capital region and memorialized that Marquis Hou Gongchen, the emperor's son-in-law, had had his father violently seize commoners' fields; he placed the matter before the law.

sentences.zh: 先是，皇子生，免天下田租三之一，獨不及皇莊及勛戚莊田。

translations.literal: Earlier, when a prince was born, one-third of the land tax nationwide was remitted, but this did not extend to imperial estates or estates of meritorious kin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when a prince was born, one-third of the land tax nationwide was remitted, but this did not extend to imperial estates or the estates of meritorious kin.

sentences.zh: 東之為言，減免如制。

translations.literal: Dongzhi spoke on the matter and reductions were granted as per regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Dongzhi spoke on the matter and reductions were granted as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 還朝，擢光祿少卿，改太仆。

translations.literal: Returning to court he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and transferred to the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to court he was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and transferred to the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 坐爭壽宮事，與李植、羊可立皆貶。

translations.literal: For disputing the mausoleum affair together with Li Zhi and Yang Keli he was demoted with them.
translations.idiomatic: For disputing the mausoleum affair together with Li Zhi and Yang Keli he was demoted with them.

sentences.zh: 東之得霍州知州，以病免。

translations.literal: Dongzhi received the post of prefect of Huozhou and retired on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Dongzhi was appointed prefect of Huozhou and retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 久之，起鄧州，進湖廣僉事。

translations.literal: After a long time he was recalled to Dengzhou and promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was recalled to Dengzhou and promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 三遷大理寺右少卿。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Right Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became Right Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，以右僉都御史巡撫貴州。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief he served as grand coordinator of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year, as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief he served as grand coordinator of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 擊高砦叛苗，斬首百余級。

translations.literal: He attacked rebellious Miao at Gaozhai and beheaded more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked rebellious Miao at Gaozhai and beheaded more than a hundred.

sentences.zh: 京察，被劾免官。

translations.literal: In the capital evaluation he was impeached and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital evaluation he was impeached and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 復以遣指揮楊國柱討楊應龍敗績事，黜為民。

translations.literal: He was again reduced to commoner status on the matter of dispatching Commander Yang Guozhu to campaign against Yang Yinglong and suffering defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He was again reduced to commoner status for dispatching Commander Yang Guozhu to campaign against Yang Yinglong and suffering defeat.

sentences.zh: 憤恨抵家卒。

translations.literal: Full of resentment he died upon reaching home.
translations.idiomatic: Full of resentment, he died upon reaching home.

sentences.zh: 東之官行人時，刑部郎舒邦儒闔門病疫死，遺孤一歲，人莫敢過其門。

translations.literal: When Dongzhi was a messenger in the Court of State Ceremonial, Bureau Director Shu Bangru's whole household died in an epidemic; an orphan of one year remained and no one dared pass his gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Dongzhi was a messenger in the Court of State Ceremonial, Bureau Director Shu Bangru's whole household died in an epidemic, leaving an orphan of one year; no one dared pass his gate.

sentences.zh: 東之經紀其喪，提其孤歸，乳之。

translations.literal: Dongzhi managed the funeral and took the orphan home to nurse him.
translations.idiomatic: Dongzhi managed the funeral, took the orphan home, and nursed him.

sentences.zh: 舒氏卒有後。

translations.literal: The Shu family ultimately had descendants.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu family ultimately had descendants.

sentences.zh: 湯兆京，字伯閎，宜興人。

translations.literal: Tang Zhaojing, style Bohong, was a native of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Zhaojing, styled Bohong, came from Yixing.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twentieth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twentieth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 除豐城知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 治最，征授御史。

translations.literal: His governance was rated the best; he was summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: His governance was rated the best; he was summoned and appointed censor.

sentences.zh: 連劾禮部侍郎朱國祚、薊遼總督萬世德，帝不問。

translations.literal: He successively impeached Vice Minister of Rites Zhu Guozuo and Liaodong Grand Coordinator Wan Shide; the emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: He successively impeached Vice Minister of Rites Zhu Guozuo and Liaodong Grand Coordinator Wan Shide; the emperor took no notice.

sentences.zh: 巡視西城，貴妃宮閹豎塗辱禮部侍郎敖文禎，兆京彈劾，杖配南京。

translations.literal: Inspecting the western ward, he found the consort's palace eunuchs had abused Vice Minister of Rites Ao Wenzhen; Zhaojing impeached them and they were beaten and sent to Nanjing in exile.
translations.idiomatic: While inspecting the western ward, he found eunuchs of the consort's palace had abused Vice Minister of Rites Ao Wenzhen; Zhaojing impeached them and they were beaten and exiled to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 時礦稅繁興，奸人競言利。

translations.literal: At that time mining taxes proliferated and schemers vied to speak of profit.
translations.idiomatic: At that time mining taxes proliferated and schemers vied to speak of profit.

sentences.zh: 有謂開海外機易山，歲可獲金四十萬者，有請征徽、寧諸府契稅，鬻高淳諸縣草場者，帝意俱向之。

translations.literal: Some said opening Mount Jiayi overseas could yield four hundred thousand taels of gold yearly; some asked to levy deed taxes in Huizhou and Ning regions and sell pasturelands in Gaochun and other counties—the emperor was inclined to all.
translations.idiomatic: Some said opening Mount Jiayi overseas could yield four hundred thousand taels of gold a year; others asked to levy deed taxes in the Huizhou and Ning regions and sell pasturelands in Gaochun and other counties—the emperor was inclined to approve them all.

sentences.zh: 兆京偕同官金忠士、史學遷、溫如璋交章力諫，不報。

translations.literal: Zhaojing together with Jin Zhongshi, Shi Xueqian, and Wen Ruzhang submitted successive memorials protesting forcefully; no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaojing, together with his colleagues Jin Zhongshi, Shi Xueqian, and Wen Ruzhang, submitted successive memorials in forceful protest; no reply came.

sentences.zh: 出按宣府、大同，請罷稅使張曄、礦使王虎、王忠，亦不納。

translations.literal: Going out to inspect Xuanfu and Datong, he asked to abolish tax envoy Zhang Ye and mining envoys Wang Hu and Wang Zhong; this too was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: On inspection tour in Xuanfu and Datong, he asked that tax envoy Zhang Ye and mining envoys Wang Hu and Wang Zhong be abolished; this too was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 掌河南道。

translations.literal: He held the Henan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He held the Henan circuit.

sentences.zh: 佐孫丕揚典京察，所譴黜皆當，而被黜者之黨爭相攻擊。

translations.literal: Assisting Sun Piyang in conducting the capital evaluation, those censured were all fitting, but the faction of those censured attacked in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Assisting Sun Piyang in conducting the capital evaluation, those censured were all fitting, but the faction of those censured attacked in turn.

sentences.zh: 兆京亦十余疏應之。

translations.literal: Zhaojing also responded with more than ten memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaojing also responded with more than ten memorials.

sentences.zh: 其詞直，卒無以奪也。

translations.literal: His language was direct and in the end they could not prevail against him.
translations.idiomatic: His language was direct, and in the end they could not prevail against him.

sentences.zh: 詳具丕揚傳中。

translations.literal: Details are given in Piyang's biography.
translations.idiomatic: Details are given in Piyang's biography.

sentences.zh: 尋出按順天諸府。

translations.literal: Soon he went out to inspect the prefectures of Shuntian and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he went out to inspect the prefectures of Shuntian and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 守陵中官李浚誣軍民盜陵木，逮系無虛日。

translations.literal: Tomb-guarding eunuch Li Jun falsely charged military and civilians with stealing tomb timber and arrested people daily without pause.
translations.idiomatic: Tomb-guarding eunuch Li Jun falsely charged soldiers and civilians with stealing tomb timber and arrested people day after day.

sentences.zh: 兆京按宣府時奏之，浚亦誣訐兆京。

translations.literal: Zhaojing had memorialized on this when inspecting Xuanfu; Jun also slandered Zhaojing in return.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaojing had memorialized on this when inspecting Xuanfu; Jun also slandered Zhaojing in return.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使按驗，事已白，而諸被系者猶未釋，兆京悉縱遣之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to investigate; though the affair was cleared, those still detained were not released; Zhaojing released them all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to investigate; though the affair was cleared, those still detained were not released; Zhaojing released them all.

sentences.zh: 東廠太監盧受縱其下橫都市，兆京論如法。

translations.literal: Eastern Depot Director Lu Shou let his subordinates run riot in the markets; Zhaojing prosecuted them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Depot Director Lu Shou let his subordinates run riot in the markets; Zhaojing prosecuted them according to law.

sentences.zh: 還復掌河南道。

translations.literal: Returning he again held the Henan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he again held the Henan circuit.

sentences.zh: 福王久不之國，兆京倡給事御史伏闕固請，卒不得命。

translations.literal: The Prince of Fu long delayed going to his fief; Zhaojing led supervising secretaries and censors in kneeling at the gate to petition firmly; in the end they could not obtain the order.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Fu long delayed going to his fief; Zhaojing led supervising secretaries and censors in kneeling at the palace gate to petition firmly, but in the end they could not obtain the order.

sentences.zh: 南京缺提學御史，吏部尚書趙煥調浙江巡按呂圖南補之，尋以年例出三御史於外，皆不咨都察院。

translations.literal: When Nanjing lacked a censor for education, Minister Zhao Huan transferred Zhejiang Investigating Censor Lü Tunan to fill it; soon by the annual rule three censors were sent outside without consulting the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanjing lacked a censor for education, Minister Zhao Huan transferred Zhejiang Investigating Censor Lü Tunan to fill the post; soon, by annual rule, three censors were sent outside without consulting the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 兆京引故事爭。

translations.literal: Zhaojing cited precedent and protested.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaojing cited precedent and protested.

sentences.zh: 圖南之調，為給事中周永春所劾，棄官歸。

translations.literal: Tunan's transfer had been impeached by Supervising Secretary Zhou Yongchun, who abandoned office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Tunan's transfer was impeached by Supervising Secretary Zhou Yongchun, who then abandoned office and returned home.

sentences.zh: 兆京及御史王時熙、汪有功為圖南申雪，語侵永春，並及煥，二人連章辨，兆京亦爭之強。

translations.literal: Zhaojing and Censors Wang Shixi and Wang Yougong cleared Tunan's name, with language impinging on Yongchun and extending to Huan; the two submitted successive defenses and Zhaojing argued fiercely as well.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaojing and Censors Wang Shixi and Wang Yougong cleared Tunan's name, with language that touched Yongchun and extended to Huan; the two submitted successive defenses and Zhaojing argued fiercely as well.

sentences.zh: 帝欲安煥，為稍奪兆京俸。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to reassure Huan and slightly docked Zhaojing's salary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to reassure Huan and slightly docked Zhaojing's salary.

sentences.zh: 兆京以不得其職，拜疏徑歸。

translations.literal: Zhaojing, unable to carry out his duties, submitted a memorial and went straight home.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to carry out his duties, Zhaojing submitted a memorial and went straight home.

sentences.zh: 御史李邦華、周起元、孫居相遂助兆京攻煥。

translations.literal: Censors Li Banghua, Zhou Qiyuan, and Sun Juxiang then aided Zhaojing in attacking Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Li Banghua, Zhou Qiyuan, and Sun Juxiang then aided Zhaojing in attacking Huan.

sentences.zh: 帝亦奪其俸，然煥亦引去。

translations.literal: The emperor also docked their salaries, yet Huan also resigned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also docked their salaries, yet Huan resigned as well.

sentences.zh: 兆京居官廉正，遇事慷慨。

translations.literal: Zhaojing in office was upright and incorrupt; encountering affairs he was passionate and bold.
translations.idiomatic: In office Zhaojing was upright and incorrupt; when affairs arose he was passionate and bold.

sentences.zh: 其時黨勢已成，正人多見齮龁。

translations.literal: By then factional power had taken shape and upright men were often harmed.
translations.idiomatic: By then factional power had taken shape and upright men were often harmed.

sentences.zh: 兆京力維持其間，清議倚以為重。

translations.literal: Zhaojing strove to uphold the balance among them, and pure criticism relied on him as its weight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaojing strove to uphold the balance among them, and pure criticism relied on him as its anchor.

sentences.zh: 屢遭排擊，卒無能一言汙之者。

translations.literal: Though repeatedly attacked, in the end no one could besmirch him with a single word.
translations.idiomatic: Though repeatedly attacked, in the end no one could besmirch him with a single word.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，贈太僕少卿。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign he was posthumously granted Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianqi reign he was posthumously granted Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 金士衡，字秉中，長洲人。

translations.literal: Jin Shiheng, style Bingzhong, was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Shiheng, styled Bingzhong, came from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 父應徵，雲南參政，以廉能稱。

translations.literal: His father Yingzheng, Yunnan administrative commissioner, was known for integrity and ability.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yingzheng, administrative commissioner in Yunnan, was known for integrity and ability.

sentences.zh: 士衡舉萬歷二十年進士，授永豐知縣，擢南京工科給事中。

translations.literal: Shiheng passed the jinshi in the twentieth year of Wanli, was appointed magistrate of Yongfeng, and was promoted to Nanjing supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng passed the jinshi in the twentieth year of the Wanli reign, was appointed magistrate of Yongfeng, and was promoted to Nanjing supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 疏陳礦稅之害，言：「曩者采於山，榷於市，今則不山而采，不市而榷矣。

translations.literal: He memorialized on the harm of mining taxes, saying: Formerly mining was in the mountains and levies in the markets; now there is mining without mountains and levying without markets.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on the harm of mining taxes, writing: 'Formerly ore was mined in the mountains and levies collected in the markets; now there is mining without mountains and levying without markets.

sentences.zh: 刑余小醜，市井無藉，安知遠謀，假以利柄，貪饕無厭。

translations.literal: Petty castrated creatures, market riffraff—how would they know far-reaching plans? Lent the power to profit, their greed is insatiable.
translations.idiomatic: Petty castrated creatures and market riffraff—how would they know far-reaching plans? Lent the power to profit, their greed knows no bounds.

sentences.zh: 楊榮啟釁於麗江，高淮肆毒於遼左，孫朝造患於石嶺，其尤著者也。

translations.literal: Yang Rong stirred strife at Lijiang, Gao Huai ran riot in eastern Liaodong, Sun Chao caused calamity at Shiling—these are the most notorious.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Rong stirred trouble at Lijiang, Gao Huai ran riot in eastern Liaodong, and Sun Chao caused calamity at Shiling—these are the most notorious examples.

sentences.zh: 今天下水旱盜賊，所在而有。

translations.literal: Under heaven today flood, drought, and bandits exist wherever one goes.
translations.idiomatic: Under heaven today, flood, drought, and bandits exist everywhere.

sentences.zh: 蕭、碭、豐、沛間河流決堤，居人為魚鱉，乃復橫征巧取以蹙之。

translations.literal: Between Xiao, Dang, Feng, and Pei river dikes burst; inhabitants became fish and turtles, yet again they were harshly taxed and cleverly squeezed to tighten the pressure.
translations.idiomatic: Between Xiao, Dang, Feng, and Pei the river dikes burst and the inhabitants were drowned like fish and turtles—yet they were harshly taxed and cleverly squeezed all the tighter.

sentences.zh: 獸窮則攫，鳥窮則啄，禍將有不可言者。」

translations.literal: When beasts are cornered they claw; when birds are cornered they peck—disaster will become beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: When beasts are cornered they claw; when birds are cornered they peck—disaster will become beyond telling.

sentences.zh: 甘肅地震，復上疏曰：「往者湖廣冰雹，順天晝晦，豐潤地陷，四川星變，遼東天鼓震，山東、山西則牛妖，人妖、今甘肅天鳴地裂，山崩川竭矣。

translations.literal: Gansu had an earthquake; he again memorialized, saying: Formerly Hubei had hail, Shuntian had daytime darkness, Fengrun had ground collapse, Sichuan had stellar anomalies, Liaodong had sky-drum thunder, Shandong and Shanxi had bovine and human omens—and now Gansu has heaven-sounds and earth-splitting, mountains collapsing and rivers drying up.
translations.idiomatic: When Gansu suffered an earthquake, he memorialized again, writing: 'Formerly Hubei had hail, Shuntian had daytime darkness, Fengrun had ground collapse, Sichuan had stellar anomalies, Liaodong had sky-drum thunder, Shandong and Shanxi had bovine and human omens—and now in Gansu heaven sounds and earth splits, mountains collapse and rivers run dry.

sentences.zh: 陛下明知亂徵，而泄泄從事，是以天下戲也。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty clearly knows the signs of disorder yet proceeds complacently—thus the realm is mocked.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty clearly sees the signs of disorder yet proceeds complacently—thus the realm is mocked.'

sentences.zh: 因極言邊糈告匱，宜急出內帑濟餉，罷撤稅使，毋事掊克，引鹿臺、西園為戒。

translations.literal: He urgently argued that border provisions were exhausted, that the inner treasury should quickly fund rations, tax commissioners be abolished, squeezing of the people cease, citing Lutai and Xiyuan as warnings.
translations.idiomatic: He urgently argued that border provisions were exhausted, that the inner treasury should quickly fund rations, tax commissioners be abolished, and the people no longer squeezed—citing Lutai and Xiyuan as warnings.

sentences.zh: 帝皆不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not heed any of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed any of it.

sentences.zh: 南京督儲尚書王基、雲南巡撫陳用賓拾遺被劾，給事中錢夢臯、御史張以渠等考察被黜，為沈一貫所庇，帝皆留之。

translations.literal: Nanjing grain-intendant Minister Wang Ji and Yunnan Grand Coordinator Chen Yongbin were impeached for remonstrance lapses; Supervising Secretary Qian Menggao, Censor Zhang Yiqu, and others were dismissed on inspection—all shielded by Shen Yiguan; the emperor kept them all.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing grain-intendant Minister Wang Ji and Yunnan Grand Coordinator Chen Yongbin were impeached for remonstrance lapses; Supervising Secretary Qian Menggao, Censor Zhang Yiqu, and others were dismissed on inspection—all shielded by Shen Yiguan, and the emperor kept them all.

sentences.zh: 士衡疏爭。

translations.literal: Shiheng memorialized in protest.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng memorialized in protest.

sentences.zh: 侍郎周應賓、黃汝良、李廷機當預推內閣。

translations.literal: Vice Ministers Zhou Yingbin, Huang Ruliang, and Li Tingji were due for preliminary recommendation to the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Ministers Zhou Yingbin, Huang Ruliang, and Li Tingji were due for preliminary recommendation to the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 士衡以不協人望，抗章論。

translations.literal: Shiheng, on grounds they did not match public expectations, submitted a defiant memorial disputing them.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng, arguing they did not match public expectations, submitted a defiant memorial disputing the nominations.

sentences.zh: 姜士昌、宋燾言事得罪，並申救之。

translations.literal: Jiang Shichang and Song Tao had offended by speaking on affairs; he also pleaded for their rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shichang and Song Tao had offended by speaking on affairs; he also pleaded for their rescue.

sentences.zh: 給事中王元翰言軍國機密不宜抄傳，詔並禁章奏未下者。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wang Yuanhan said military and state secrets should not be copied and transmitted; an edict also forbade memorials not yet issued.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Wang Yuanhan said military and state secrets should not be copied and transmitted; an edict also forbade circulating memorials not yet issued.

sentences.zh: 由是中朝政事，四方寂然不得聞。

translations.literal: From this, court affairs at the center were unknown in silence throughout the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: From this, affairs at the center of government fell silent throughout the realm and could no longer be heard.

sentences.zh: 士衡力陳其非便。

translations.literal: Shiheng forcefully argued against the inconvenience.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng forcefully argued that this was harmful.

sentences.zh: 疏多不行。

translations.literal: Most of his memorials went unimplemented.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his memorials went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 帝召王錫爵為首輔，以被劾奏辨，語過憤激，士衡馳疏劾之。

translations.literal: The emperor recalled Wang Xijue as chief grand secretary; defending himself against impeachment with overly angry language, Shiheng urgently memorialized to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor recalled Wang Xijue as chief grand secretary; defending himself against impeachment in overly angry language, Shiheng urgently memorialized to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 尋擢南京通政參議。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Nanjing Assistant Director of the Court of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Nanjing Assistant Director of the Court of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 時元翰及李三才先後為言者所攻，士衡並為申雪。

translations.literal: At the time Yuanhan and Li Sancai were successively attacked by memorialists; Shiheng cleared both their names.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yuanhan and Li Sancai were successively attacked by memorialists; Shiheng cleared both their names.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，大計京官。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year, the major evaluation of capital officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year came the major evaluation of capital officials.

sentences.zh: 掌南察者，南京吏部侍郎史繼偕，齊、楚、浙人之黨也，與孫丕揚北察相反，凡助三才、元翰者悉斥之。

translations.literal: In charge of southern inspection was Nanjing Vice Minister of Personnel Shi Jixie, of the Qi-Chu-Zhe faction, opposed to Sun Piyang's northern inspection; all who had aided Sancai and Yuanhan were expelled.
translations.idiomatic: In charge of southern inspection was Nanjing Vice Minister of Personnel Shi Jixie, of the Qi-Chu-Zhe faction, opposed to Sun Piyang's northern inspection; all who had aided Sancai and Yuanhan were expelled.

sentences.zh: 士衡亦謫兩浙鹽運副使，不赴。

translations.literal: Shiheng was also demoted to Vice Salt Transport Commissioner for the Two Zhes; he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng was also demoted to Vice Salt Transport Commissioner for the Two Zhes; he did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，起兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianqi he was raised to Vice Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianqi reign he was raised to Vice Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 累遷太僕少卿。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 引疾去，卒於家。

translations.literal: Citing illness he resigned; he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Citing illness he resigned and died at home.

sentences.zh: 先是，楊應龍伏誅，貴州宣慰使安疆臣邀據故所侵地。

translations.literal: Previously, after Yang Yinglong was executed, Guizhou Pacification Commissioner An Jiangchen opportunistically seized lands he had formerly encroached upon.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, after Yang Yinglong was executed, Guizhou Pacification Commissioner An Jiangchen opportunistically seized the lands he had formerly encroached upon.

sentences.zh: 總督王象乾不許。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Wang Xiangqian did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Wang Xiangqian did not permit it.

sentences.zh: 士衡遂劾象乾起釁。

translations.literal: Shiheng then impeached Xiangqian for starting a quarrel.
translations.idiomatic: Shiheng then impeached Xiangqian for starting the quarrel.

sentences.zh: 後象乾弟象恒巡撫蘇、松，以兄故頗銜士衡。

translations.literal: Later Xiangqian's brother Xiangheng, grand coordinator of Suzhou and Songjiang, bore considerable resentment toward Shiheng because of his brother.
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiangqian's brother Xiangheng, grand coordinator of Suzhou and Songjiang, bore considerable resentment toward Shiheng because of his brother.

sentences.zh: 廉知其清介狀，稱說不置雲。

translations.literal: Learning of his integrity and upright character, he praised him without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of his integrity and upright character, he praised him without cease.

sentences.zh: 王元翰，字伯舉，雲南寧州人。

translations.literal: Wang Yuanhan, style Boju, was a native of Ningzhou in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuanhan, styled Boju, came from Ningzhou in Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十九年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the twenty-ninth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the twenty-ninth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 選庶吉士。

translations.literal: Selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，改吏科給事中。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year he was transferred to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year he was transferred to supervising secretary in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 意氣陵厲，以諫諍自任。

translations.literal: His spirit was fierce and overbearing; he took remonstrance as his duty.
translations.idiomatic: His spirit was fierce and overbearing; he took remonstrance as his duty.

sentences.zh: 時廷臣習偷惰，法度盡弛。

translations.literal: At the time court ministers had grown accustomed to laziness and slackness; regulations were wholly relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time court ministers had grown accustomed to laziness and slackness, and regulations were wholly relaxed.

sentences.zh: 會推之柄散在九列科道。

translations.literal: The power of collective recommendation was scattered among the nine ranks and the censorate and supervising secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: The power of collective recommendation was scattered among the nine ministerial ranks and the censorate and supervising secretaries.

sentences.zh: 率推京卿，每署數倍舊額。

translations.literal: They generally recommended capital ministers, each list several times the old quota.
translations.idiomatic: They generally recommended capital ministers, each list several times the old quota.

sentences.zh: 而建言諸臣，一斥不復。

translations.literal: Yet memorializing ministers, once dismissed, never returned.
translations.idiomatic: Yet memorializing ministers, once dismissed, never returned.

sentences.zh: 大臣被彈，率連章詆訐。

translations.literal: When grand ministers were impeached, they generally submitted successive memorials of slander.
translations.idiomatic: When grand ministers were impeached, they generally submitted successive memorials of slander.

sentences.zh: 元翰悉疏論其非。

translations.literal: Yuanhan memorialized on all these wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhan memorialized against all of these abuses.

sentences.zh: 尋進工科右給事中，巡視廠庫，極陳惜薪司官多之害。

translations.literal: Soon promoted to Right Supervising Secretary in the Ministry of Works; inspecting factory storehouses, he urgently argued the harm of too many officials in the Firewood Office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon promoted to Right Supervising Secretary in the Ministry of Works, he inspected factory storehouses and urgently argued the harm of too many officials in the Firewood Office.

sentences.zh: 其秋上疏，極言時事敗壞，請帝昧爽視朝，廷見大臣，言官得隨其後，日陳四方利病。

translations.literal: That autumn he memorialized, urgently stating affairs were ruined, asking the emperor to hold court at dawn, receive ministers in audience, let remonstrance officials follow, and daily present the ills and benefits of the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he memorialized, urgently stating that affairs were ruined, asking the emperor to hold court at dawn, receive ministers in audience, let remonstrance officials follow, and daily present the ills and benefits of the four directions.

sentences.zh: 尋復陳時事，言：「輔臣，心膂也。

translations.literal: Soon again he presented on current affairs, saying: Grand secretaries are the heart and sinew.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he again presented on current affairs, writing: 'Grand secretaries are the heart and sinew of the state.

sentences.zh: 朱賡輔政三載，猶未一覯天顏，可痛哭者一。

translations.literal: Zhu Geng has assisted government three years yet has not once beheld the imperial countenance—this is the first cause for weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Geng has assisted government for three years yet has not once beheld the imperial countenance—this is the first cause for weeping.

sentences.zh: 九卿強半虛懸，甚者闔署無一人。

translations.literal: Of the nine ministers more than half their posts are empty; in extreme cases entire offices have not a single person.
translations.idiomatic: More than half the posts among the nine ministers are empty; in extreme cases entire offices have not a single person.

sentences.zh: 監司、郡守，亦曠年無官，或一人綰數符。

translations.literal: Circuit intendants and prefects also go years without officials, or one man holds several seals.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit intendants and prefects also go years without officials, or one man holds several seals.

sentences.zh: 事不切身，政自茍且，可痛哭者二。

translations.literal: Affairs not touching one's person, government naturally becomes perfunctory—this is the second cause for weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Because affairs do not touch one's person, government naturally becomes perfunctory—this is the second cause for weeping.

sentences.zh: 兩都臺省寥寥幾人。

translations.literal: At the two capitals the censorate and secretariat have scarcely a few men.
translations.idiomatic: At the two capitals the censorate and secretariat have scarcely a few men.

sentences.zh: 行取入都者，累年不被命。

translations.literal: Those selected by promotion exam for the capital go years without appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Those selected by promotion exam for the capital go years without appointment.

sentences.zh: 庶常散館亦越常期。

translations.literal: Hanlin bachelors leaving the academy also exceed the usual term.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin bachelors leaving the academy also exceed the usual term.

sentences.zh: 御史巡方事竣，遣代無人。

translations.literal: When regional censors finish their tours, no one is sent to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: When regional censors finish their tours, no one is sent to replace them.

sentences.zh: 威令不行，上下胥玩，可痛哭者三。

translations.literal: Authority and orders are not enforced; upper and lower all treat affairs lightly—this is the third cause for weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Authority and orders are not enforced; upper and lower all treat affairs lightly—this is the third cause for weeping.

sentences.zh: 被廢諸臣，久淪山谷。

translations.literal: Dismissed ministers long languish in mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed ministers long languish in mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 近雖奉詔敘錄，未見連茹匯征。

translations.literal: Recently though an edict ordered their reinstatement, one does not see them gathered like gourds on a vine and summoned together.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, though an edict ordered their reinstatement, one does not see them gathered like gourds on a vine and summoned together.

sentences.zh: 茍更閱數年，日漸銷鑠。

translations.literal: If several more years pass, they will daily wane and melt away.
translations.idiomatic: If several more years pass, they will daily wane and fade away.

sentences.zh: 人之雲亡，邦國殄瘁，可痛哭者四。

translations.literal: As men are lost, the state is wasted and afflicted—this is the fourth cause for weeping.
translations.idiomatic: As men are lost, the state is wasted and afflicted—this is the fourth cause for weeping.

sentences.zh: 九邊歲餉，缺至八十余萬，平居凍餒，脫巾可虞；

translations.literal: Nine-border annual pay falls short by more than eight hundred thousand; in normal times they freeze and starve, mutiny is to be feared;
translations.idiomatic: Nine-border annual pay falls short by more than eight hundred thousand; in normal times the troops freeze and starve, and mutiny is to be feared;

sentences.zh: 有事怨憤，死綏無望。

translations.literal: In crisis they resent and rage, with no hope of dying loyally in service.
translations.idiomatic: in crisis they resent and rage, with no hope of dying loyally in service.

sentences.zh: 塞北之患，未可知也。

translations.literal: Trouble on the northern frontier cannot be foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: Trouble on the northern frontier cannot be foreseen.

sentences.zh: 京師十余萬兵，歲靡餉二百余萬，大都市井負販遊手而已。

translations.literal: The capital's hundred thousand-odd troops consume more than two million in annual pay—great city peddlers and idlers, nothing more.
