translations.idiomatic: The capital's hundred thousand-odd troops consume more than two million in annual pay—they are great-city peddlers and idlers, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 一旦有急，能驅使赴敵哉？

translations.literal: Once emergency comes, can they be driven to face the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: Once emergency comes, can they be driven to face the enemy?

sentences.zh: 可痛哭者五。

translations.literal: This is the fifth cause for weeping.
translations.idiomatic: This is the fifth cause for weeping.

sentences.zh: 天子高拱深居，所恃以通下情者，只章疏耳，今一切高閣。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sits high and deep within; the only means to communicate lower feelings is memorials—now all are shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven sits high and deep within; the only means to communicate the feelings of those below is memorials—and now all are shelved.

sentences.zh: 慷慨建白者莫不曰『吾知無濟，第存此議論耳』。

translations.literal: Bold memorialists all say: I know it will not help; I merely preserve this opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Bold memorialists all say: 'I know it will not help; I merely preserve this opinion.'

sentences.zh: 言路惟空存議論，世道何如哉！

translations.literal: The remonstrance path holds only empty opinions—what has become of the age!
translations.idiomatic: The remonstrance path holds only empty opinions—what has become of the age!

sentences.zh: 可痛哭者六。

translations.literal: This is the sixth cause for weeping.
translations.idiomatic: This is the sixth cause for weeping.

sentences.zh: 榷稅使者滿天下，致小民怨聲徹天，降災召異。

translations.literal: Tax commissioners fill the realm, driving the people's cries of resentment to heaven, bringing down disasters and summoning anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: Tax commissioners fill the realm, driving the common people's cries of resentment to heaven and bringing down disasters and omens.

sentences.zh: 方且指殿工以為名，借停止以愚眾。

translations.literal: Yet they point to palace construction as their pretext and use pretended halts to fool the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they point to palace construction as their pretext and use pretended halts to fool the masses.

sentences.zh: 是天以回祿警陛下，陛下反以回祿剝萬民也。

translations.literal: Heaven uses conflagration to warn Your Majesty, yet Your Majesty uses conflagration to strip the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven uses conflagration to warn Your Majesty, yet Your Majesty uses conflagration to strip the myriad people.

sentences.zh: 眾心離叛，而猶不知變，可痛哭者七。

translations.literal: Popular hearts turn away in rebellion yet still there is no knowing to change—this is the seventh cause for weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Popular hearts turn away in rebellion, yet still there is no knowing to change—this is the seventh cause for weeping.

sentences.zh: 郊廟不親，則天地祖宗不相屬；

translations.literal: Not personally attending suburban and temple rites, then Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples are not connected;
translations.idiomatic: Not personally attending suburban and temple rites, then Heaven, Earth, and the ancestral temples are not connected;

sentences.zh: 朝講不禦，則伏機隱禍不上聞。

translations.literal: Not holding court lectures, then hidden schemes and concealed calamities are not heard above.
translations.idiomatic: Not holding court lectures, then hidden schemes and concealed calamities are not heard above.

sentences.zh: 古今未有如此而天下無事者。

translations.literal: Never in antiquity or the present has the realm been untroubled with such things.
translations.idiomatic: Never in antiquity or the present has the realm been untroubled with such things.

sentences.zh: 且青宮輟講，亦已經年，親宦官宮妾，而疏正人端士，獨奈何不為宗社計也！

translations.literal: Moreover the Eastern Palace has suspended lectures for years already, favoring eunuchs and palace women while keeping distant upright gentlemen—how can you alone fail to reckon for the altars of state!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Eastern Palace has suspended lectures for years already, favoring eunuchs and palace women while keeping distant upright gentlemen—how can you alone fail to reckon for the altars of state!

sentences.zh: 可痛哭者八。」

translations.literal: This is the eighth cause for weeping.
translations.idiomatic: This is the eighth cause for weeping.

sentences.zh: 帝皆不省。

translations.literal: The emperor paid no heed to any of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor paid no heed to any of it.

sentences.zh: 武定賊阿克作亂。

translations.literal: The bandit Ake of Wuding rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Ake of Wuding rebelled.

sentences.zh: 元翰上言：「克本小醜，亂易平也。

translations.literal: Yuanhan submitted: Ke is originally a petty villain; the disorder is easily pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhan submitted: 'Ke is originally a petty villain; the disorder is easily pacified.

sentences.zh: 至雲南大害，莫甚貢金、榷稅二事。

translations.literal: As for Yunnan's great harm, nothing exceeds tribute gold and tax levies.
translations.idiomatic: As for Yunnan's great harm, nothing exceeds tribute gold and tax levies.

sentences.zh: 民不堪命，至殺稅使，而征榷如故。

translations.literal: The people cannot bear their lives; they even kill tax commissioners, yet levies continue as before.
translations.idiomatic: The people cannot bear their lives; they even kill tax commissioners, yet levies continue as before.

sentences.zh: 貢金請減，反增益之。

translations.literal: When tribute gold was requested to be reduced, it was instead increased.
translations.idiomatic: When tribute gold was requested to be reduced, it was instead increased.

sentences.zh: 眾心憤怒，使亂賊假以為名。

translations.literal: Popular hearts rage with anger, letting rebels borrow this as their justification.
translations.idiomatic: Popular hearts rage with anger, letting rebels borrow this as their justification.

sentences.zh: 賊首縱撲滅，虐政不除，滇之為滇，猶未可保也。」

translations.literal: Even if the rebel chief is crushed, if cruel government is not removed, whether Yunnan can remain Yunnan is still uncertain.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the rebel chief is crushed, if cruel government is not removed, whether Yunnan can remain Yunnan is still uncertain.

sentences.zh: 俄言：「礦稅之設，本為大工。

translations.literal: Soon he said: Mining taxes were established originally for great construction.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he said: 'Mining taxes were established originally for great construction.

sentences.zh: 若捐內帑數百萬金，工可立竣，毋徒苦四方萬姓。」

translations.literal: If several million from the inner treasury were donated, the work could be quickly finished—do not vainly torment the myriad people of the four directions.
translations.idiomatic: If several million from the inner treasury were donated, the work could be quickly finished—do not vainly torment the myriad people of the four directions.

sentences.zh: 疏皆不報。

translations.literal: His memorials received no response.
translations.idiomatic: His memorials received no response.

sentences.zh: 尋兩疏劾貴州巡撫郭子章等凡四人，言：「子章曲庇安疆臣，堅意割地，貽西南大憂。

translations.literal: Soon in two memorials he impeached Guizhou Grand Coordinator Guo Zizhang and three others, saying: Zizhang openly shielded An Jiangchen, insisted on ceding land, bequeathing great worry to the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: Soon in two memorials he impeached Guizhou Grand Coordinator Guo Zizhang and three others, writing: 'Zizhang openly shielded An Jiangchen, insisted on ceding land, and bequeathed great worry to the southwest.

sentences.zh: 且嘗著《婦寺論》，言人主當隔絕廷臣，專與宦官宮妾處，乃相安無患。

translations.literal: Moreover he once wrote On Wives and Eunuchs, saying the ruler should cut off court ministers and keep only to eunuchs and palace women, then all would be secure without trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he once wrote On Wives and Eunuchs, saying the ruler should cut off court ministers and keep only to eunuchs and palace women, then all would be secure without trouble.

sentences.zh: 子章罪當斬。」

translations.literal: Zizhang's crime deserves decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhang's crime deserves decapitation.

sentences.zh: 不納。

translations.literal: Not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: It was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 先是，廷推閣臣。

translations.literal: Previously, court recommendation for grand secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, there was court recommendation for grand secretaries.

sentences.zh: 元翰言李廷機非宰相器。

translations.literal: Yuanhan said Li Tingji was not material for a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhan said Li Tingji was not material for a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 已而黃汝良推吏部侍郎，全天敘推南京禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon Huang Ruliang was recommended for Vice Minister of Personnel, Quan Tianxu for Nanjing Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Huang Ruliang was recommended for Vice Minister of Personnel and Quan Tianxu for Nanjing Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 汝良，廷機邑人；

translations.literal: Ruliang was Tingji's townsman;
translations.idiomatic: Ruliang was Tingji's townsman;

sentences.zh: 天敘，朱賡同鄉也。

translations.literal: Tianxu was Zhu Geng's fellow townsman.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxu was Zhu Geng's fellow townsman.

sentences.zh: 元翰極論會推之弊，譏切政府，二人遂不用。

translations.literal: Yuanhan urgently argued the evils of collective recommendation, satirizing the government sharply; the two were then not used.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhan urgently argued the evils of collective recommendation and satirized the government sharply; the two were then not used.

sentences.zh: 至是，將推兩京兵部尚書蕭大亨、孫幰為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: At this point, the Two-Capital Ministers of War Xiao Daheng and Sun Kan were to be recommended for Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At this point, the two-capital Ministers of War Xiao Daheng and Sun Kan were to be recommended for Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 元翰亦疏論二人，並言職方郎申用懋為大亨謀主，太常少卿唐鶴征為幰謀主，亦當斥。

translations.literal: Yuanhan also memorialized against the two, further saying Bureau of Appointments Director Shen Yongmao was Daheng's plot-master and Vice Director of Sacrificial Ceremonies Tang Hezheng was Kan's plot-master—they too should be expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhan also memorialized against the two, further saying Bureau of Appointments Director Shen Yongmao was Daheng's plot-master and Vice Director of Sacrificial Ceremonies Tang Hezheng was Kan's plot-master—they too should be expelled.

sentences.zh: 尋因災異，乞亟罷賡、大亨及副都御史詹沂。

translations.literal: Soon, citing calamities and portents, he begged that Geng, Daheng, and Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhan Yi be dismissed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, citing calamities and portents, he pleaded for the immediate dismissal of Zhu Geng, Quan Tianxu, and Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhan Yi.

sentences.zh: 且言：「近更有二大變。

translations.literal: Moreover he said: 'Recently there have been two great transformations.
translations.idiomatic: He went on: 'Recently there have been two great transformations.

sentences.zh: 大小臣工誌期得官，不顧嗤笑，此一變也。

translations.literal: Great and small officials set their hearts on obtaining office, heedless of ridicule—this is one transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Officials high and low are bent on winning appointments, heedless of ridicule—this is the first transformation.

sentences.zh: 陛下不恤人言，甚至天地譴告亦悍然弗顧，此又一變也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty does not heed men's words; you even defiantly disregard Heaven and Earth's reproofs—this is yet another transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty pays no heed to public opinion, and even Heaven and Earth's warnings are defiantly ignored—this is the second.

sentences.zh: 有君心之變，然後臣工之變因之。

translations.literal: When the sovereign's heart has changed, only then do the officials' transformations follow.
translations.idiomatic: Once the sovereign's heart turns, the conduct of his officials follows suit.

sentences.zh: 在今日，挽天地洪水寇賊之變易，挽君心與臣工之變難。」

translations.literal: In the present day, to turn back the transformations of Heaven-and-Earth, floods, and bandits is easy; to turn back the transformations of the sovereign's heart and the officials is hard.'
translations.idiomatic: Today it would be easy to reverse floods, banditry, and other calamities sent from Heaven and Earth—but far harder to reverse the change in the sovereign's heart and in his officials.'

sentences.zh: 又言：「陛下三十年培養之人才，半掃除於申時行、王錫爵，半禁錮於沈一貫、朱賡。」

translations.literal: He also said: 'The talent Your Majesty cultivated over thirty years—half was swept away by Shen Shixing and Wang Xijue, half imprisoned by Shen Yiguan and Zhu Geng.'
translations.idiomatic: He added: 'The talent Your Majesty cultivated over thirty years—half was swept away by Shen Shixing and Wang Xijue, half kept in confinement by Shen Yiguan and Zhu Geng.'

sentences.zh: 因薦鄒元標、顧憲成等十余人。

translations.literal: He therefore recommended Zou Yuanbiao, Gu Xiancheng, and more than ten others.
translations.idiomatic: On that basis he recommended Zou Yuanbiao, Gu Xiancheng, and more than a dozen others.

sentences.zh: 無何，又劾給事中喻安性、御史管橘敗群叢穢，皆不報。

translations.literal: Before long he again impeached Supervising Secretary Yu Anxing and Censor Guan Ju for corrupt clique filth; none received response.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he impeached Supervising Secretary Yu Anxing and Censor Guan Ju for the filth of a corrupt clique, but the court took no notice.

sentences.zh: 掌廠內官王道不法，疏暴其罪，亦弗聽。

translations.literal: The factory eunuch Wang Dao acted unlawfully; he exposed his crimes in a memorial, yet it too went unheeded.
translations.idiomatic: When the depot eunuch Wang Dao broke the law, Yuanhan exposed his crimes in a memorial, but that too was ignored.

sentences.zh: 元翰居諫垣四年，力持清議。

translations.literal: Yuanhan served four years in the remonstrance offices, forcefully upholding pure opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhan spent four years in the remonstrance offices, staunchly upholding righteous criticism.

sentences.zh: 摩主闕，拄貴近，世服其敢言。

translations.literal: He polished the sovereign's faults, braced himself against the powerful and close, and the age admired his bold speech.
translations.idiomatic: He admonished the throne on its failings, stood up to the powerful at court, and the age admired his outspoken courage.

sentences.zh: 然銳意搏擊，毛舉鷹鷙，舉朝鹹畏其口。

translations.literal: Yet he was keen to strike, nitpicking with eagle fierceness, and the whole court feared his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was eager to attack, nitpicking with hawkish ferocity, and the whole court feared his tongue.

sentences.zh: 吏科都給事中陳治則與元翰不相能，御史鄭繼芳，其門人也，遂劾元翰盜庫金，克商人貲，奸贓數十萬。

translations.literal: Chief Supervising Secretary of the Personnel Section Chen Zheze was at odds with Yuanhan; Censor Zheng Jifang, his disciple, then impeached Yuanhan for stealing treasury gold, extorting merchants' goods, and corrupt gains numbering several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zheze, chief supervising secretary of the personnel section, was at odds with Yuanhan; his disciple, Censor Zheng Jifang, then impeached Yuanhan for embezzling treasury funds, extorting merchants, and amassing corrupt gains in the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 元翰憤甚，辨疏詆繼芳北鄙小賊，語過激。

translations.literal: Yuanhan was greatly angered; in a defense memorial he reviled Jifang as a northern rustic petty thief, his language excessively sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Yuanhan replied in a defense memorial calling Jifang a petty northern rustic, in language far too inflammatory.

sentences.zh: 於是繼芳黨劉文炳、王紹徽、劉國縉等十余疏並攻之，而史記事、胡忻、史學遷、張國儒、馬孟禎、陳於廷、吳亮、金士衡、高節、劉蘭輩則連章論救。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jifang's faction—Liu Wenbing, Wang Shaohui, Liu Guojin, and more than ten others—submitted memorials attacking him together, while Shi Jishi, Hu Xin, Shi Xueqian, Zhang Guoru, Ma Mengzhen, Chen Yuting, Wu Liang, Jin Shiheng, Gao Jie, Liu Lan, and their like submitted linked memorials pleading for him.
translations.idiomatic: Jifang's allies—Liu Wenbing, Wang Shaohui, Liu Guojin, and more than ten others—then flooded the court with attacking memorials, while Shi Jishi, Hu Xin, Shi Xueqian, Zhang Guoru, Ma Mengzhen, Chen Yuting, Wu Liang, Jin Shiheng, Gao Jie, Liu Lan, and others filed linked memorials in his defense.

sentences.zh: 帝悉不省。

translations.literal: The emperor paid no heed to any of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored them all.

sentences.zh: 元翰乃盡出其筐篋，舁置國門，縱吏士簡括，慟哭辭朝而去。

translations.literal: Yuanhan then brought out everything in his chests and baskets, had it carried to the state gate, allowed officials and clerks to search and examine it, wept in grief, took leave of court, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhan then emptied every chest and basket he owned, had the goods carried to the capital gate, invited officials to search them, wept as he took leave of court, and departed.

sentences.zh: 吏部坐擅離職守，謫刑部檢校。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel punished him for leaving his post without authorization and demoted him to proofreader in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel found him guilty of abandoning his post without leave and demoted him to proofreader in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 後孫丕揚主京察，斥治則、國縉等，亦以浮躁坐元翰，再貶湖廣按察知事。

translations.literal: Later, when Sun Piyang presided over the capital evaluation, he dismissed Zheze, Guojin, and the rest, and also punished Yuanhan for flightiness, demoting him again to assistant intendant of surveillance in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Sun Piyang presided over the capital evaluation of officials, he dismissed Zheze, Guojin, and their allies, and also punished Yuanhan for rashness, demoting him again to assistant surveillance intendant in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 方繼芳之發疏也，即潛遣人圍守元翰家。

translations.literal: When Jifang had first submitted his memorial, he had secretly sent men to surround and guard Yuanhan's house.
translations.idiomatic: The moment Jifang filed his memorial, he had secretly sent men to surround Yuanhan's house.

sentences.zh: 及元翰去，所劾贓無有，則謂寄之記事家。

translations.literal: When Yuanhan departed, the corrupt gains he had been accused of were nowhere to be found; they then said he had entrusted them to Jishi's house.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanhan left, none of the bribes alleged against him could be found; his accusers then claimed he had hidden them at Jishi's home.

sentences.zh: 兩黨分爭久不息。

translations.literal: The two factions quarreled for a long time without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The two factions quarreled on without end.

sentences.zh: 而是時劾李三才者亦指其貪，諸左右元翰者又往往左右三才，由是臣僚益相水火，而朋黨之勢成矣。

translations.literal: At that time those impeaching Li Sancai also charged him with greed; those who sided with Yuanhan often sided with Sancai as well, and so the officials grew ever more mutually hostile, until the force of faction was fully formed.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time, those attacking Li Sancai charged him with corruption, while Yuanhan's allies often rallied to Sancai as well; officials grew ever more bitterly opposed, and court faction hardened into a fixed pattern.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，累遷刑部主事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he was repeatedly promoted to principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he rose through repeated promotions to principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢亂政，其黨石三畏劾之，削籍。

translations.literal: When Wei Zhongxian threw the government into disorder, his follower Shi Sanwei impeached him and he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zhongxian threw the government into chaos, his follower Shi Sanwei impeached him and he was removed from the official rolls.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝即位，復官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Sizong ascended the throne, his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor came to the throne, Yuanhan was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 將召用，為尚書王永光所尼。

translations.literal: Just as he was to be summoned back into service, Minister Wang Yongguang obstructed it.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was about to be recalled to service, Minister Wang Yongguang blocked the appointment.

sentences.zh: 元翰乃流寓南都，十年不歸。

translations.literal: Yuanhan then drifted in exile in the Southern Capital and did not return for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhan then lived in exile in Nanjing and did not return for ten years.

sentences.zh: 卒，遂葬焉。

translations.literal: When he died, he was buried there.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was buried there.

sentences.zh: 孫振基，字肖岡，潼關衛人。

translations.literal: Sun Zhenji, styled Xiaogang, was a man of Tongguan Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhenji, styled Xiaogang, was a native of Tongguan Guard.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十九年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-ninth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-ninth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 除莘縣知縣，調繁安丘。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Xin County and transferred to the demanding post of Anqiu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Xin County, then transferred to the demanding post of Anqiu.

sentences.zh: 三十六年四月，以治行征，與李成名等十七人當授給事中，先除禮部主事。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the thirty-sixth year, summoned for excellent administration, he and Li Chengming and seventeen others were to receive supervising secretary appointments; he was first appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the thirty-sixth year he was summoned to the capital for excellent administration; he and Li Chengming and sixteen others were slated for supervising secretary posts, and he was first appointed principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 四十年十月命始下，振基得戶科。

translations.literal: The order was not issued until the tenth month of the fortieth year; Zhenji received the Household Section.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment did not come through until the tenth month of the fortieth year, when Zhenji received a post in the Household Section.

sentences.zh: 時吏部推舉大僚，每患乏才，振基力請起廢。

translations.literal: At the time, whenever the Ministry of Personnel recommended high officials it often lacked talent; Zhenji forcefully petitioned to recall the dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Ministry of Personnel often found itself short of talent when recommending high officials; Zhenji forcefully petitioned to recall dismissed men to service.

sentences.zh: 韓敬者，歸安人也，受業宣城湯賓尹。

translations.literal: Han Jing was a man of Gui'an and had studied under Tang Binyin of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jing, a native of Gui'an, had studied under Tang Binyin of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 賓尹分校會試，敬卷為他考官所棄。

translations.literal: When Binyin graded the metropolitan examination, Jing's paper was discarded by another examiner.
translations.idiomatic: When Binyin served as an examiner for the metropolitan examination, Jing's paper had been rejected by another grader.

sentences.zh: 賓尹搜得之，強總裁侍郎蕭雲舉、王圖錄為第一。

translations.literal: Binyin searched it out and forcibly had Vice Presidents Xiao Yunju and Wang Tu record it as first place.
translations.idiomatic: Binyin hunted it down and forced the chief examiners, Vice Presidents Xiao Yunju and Wang Tu, to rank it first.

sentences.zh: 榜發，士論大嘩。

translations.literal: When the list was published, opinion among the literati erupted.
translations.idiomatic: When the results were posted, educated opinion erupted in outrage.

sentences.zh: 知貢舉侍郎吳道南欲奏之，以雲舉、圖資深，嫌擠排前輩，隱不發。

translations.literal: Vice President Wu Daonan, who oversaw the examination, wished to memorialize the matter, but because Yunju and Tu were senior he feared appearing to squeeze out his elders and kept silent.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Daonan, the vice president overseeing the examination, wanted to report the affair, but Yunju and Tu were senior men and he feared seeming to attack his elders, so he kept silent.

sentences.zh: 及廷對，賓尹為敬夤緣得第一人。

translations.literal: At the palace examination, Binyin pulled strings so that Jing received first place.
translations.idiomatic: At the palace examination Binyin pulled strings so that Jing won first place.

sentences.zh: 後賓尹以考察褫官，敬亦稱病去，事三年矣。

translations.literal: Later Binyin was dismissed from office in the regular evaluation, and Jing also pleaded illness and withdrew; three years had passed since the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Later Binyin was stripped of office in the regular evaluation, and Jing also pleaded illness and withdrew; three years had passed since the scandal.

sentences.zh: 會進士鄒之麟分校順天鄉試，所取童學賢有私，於是御史孫居相並賓尹事發之。

translations.literal: It happened that the jinshi Zou Zhilin graded the Shuntian provincial examination and showed favoritism in selecting Tong Xuexian; Censor Sun Juxiang then exposed both Binyin's affair and this one.
translations.idiomatic: When the jinshi Zou Zhilin graded the Shuntian provincial examination and showed favoritism toward Tong Xuexian, Censor Sun Juxiang exposed both that case and Binyin's earlier scandal.

sentences.zh: 下禮官，會吏部都察院議，顧不及賓尹事。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the Ministry of Rites; the Ministry of Personnel and the Censorate met to discuss it, yet deliberately omitted Binyin's affair.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was sent to the Ministry of Rites, and the Ministry of Personnel and Censorate met to discuss it—but deliberately left Binyin's case out.

sentences.zh: 振基乃抗疏請並議，未得命。

translations.literal: Zhenji then submitted a forceful memorial asking that it be discussed together; he received no answer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenji then submitted a forceful memorial demanding that Binyin's case be included; the court gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎翁正春等議黜學賢，謫之麟，亦不及賓尹等。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Weng Zhengchun and others recommended dismissing Xuexian and demoting Zhilin, but again did not reach Binyin and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Rites Weng Zhengchun and others recommended dismissing Xuexian and demoting Zhilin, but again stopped short of Binyin and his allies.

sentences.zh: 振基謂議者庇之，再疏論劾。

translations.literal: Zhenji said the deliberators were shielding them and submitted another memorial of impeachment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenji charged that the deliberators were shielding the guilty and filed a second impeachment memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝乃下廷臣更議。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered the court officials to reconsider.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered the court to reconsider.

sentences.zh: 御史王時熙、劉策、馬孟禎亦疏論其事，而南京給事中張篤敬證尤力。

translations.literal: Censors Wang Shixi, Liu Ce, and Ma Mengzhen also memorialized on the affair, while Nanjing Supervising Secretary Zhang Dujing testified with especial force.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Wang Shixi, Liu Ce, and Ma Mengzhen also memorialized on the case, while Nanjing Supervising Secretary Zhang Dujing bore witness with especial force.

sentences.zh: 方賓尹之分校也，越房取中五人，他考官效之，競相搜取，凡十七人。

translations.literal: When Binyin was grading examinations, he crossed rooms and passed five men; other examiners copied him, competing to search out papers, seventeen men in all.
translations.idiomatic: When Binyin graded examinations he crossed into other examiners' rooms and passed five candidates; other graders copied him, competing to pull favored papers, seventeen men in all.

sentences.zh: 時賓尹雖廢，中朝多其黨，欲藉是寬敬。

translations.literal: At the time, though Binyin had been dismissed, the inner court had many of his partisans, who wished to use this to leniently treat Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Though Binyin had already been dismissed, many of his allies remained at court and hoped to use the broader scandal to soften the punishment of Jing.

sentences.zh: 正春乃會九卿趙煥及都給事中翁憲祥、御史余懋衡等六十三人議坐敬不謹，落職閑住。

translations.literal: Zhengchun then convened the Nine Ministers, Zhao Huan, Chief Supervising Secretary Weng Xianxiang, Censor Yu Maoheng, and sixty-three others, who decided to punish Jing for lack of care and dismiss him to idle residence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengchun then convened Zhao Huan, the Nine Ministers, Chief Supervising Secretary Weng Xianxiang, Censor Yu Maoheng, and sixty-three others, who decided to punish Jing for negligence and dismiss him to idle residence.

sentences.zh: 御史劉廷元、董元儒、過庭訓，敬同鄉也，謂敬關節果真，罪非止不謹，執不署名，意欲遷延為敬地。

translations.literal: Censors Liu Tingyuan, Dong Yuanru, and Guo Tingxun were Jing's fellow townsmen; they said Jing's exam fraud was real and the crime was more than mere lack of care, refused to sign, and intended to delay matters to make room for Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Liu Tingyuan, Dong Yuanru, and Guo Tingxun were Jing's fellow townsmen; they argued that his exam fraud was genuine and the offense went beyond negligence, refused to sign, and hoped to stall the case in Jing's favor.

sentences.zh: 正春等不從，持初議上。

translations.literal: Zhengchun and the rest would not agree and submitted the original recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengchun and the others would not yield and submitted their original recommendation.

sentences.zh: 廷元遂疏劾之，公議益憤。

translations.literal: Tingyuan then memorialized to impeach them, and public opinion grew ever angrier.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyuan then filed an impeachment memorial against them, and public outrage only grew.

sentences.zh: 振基、居相、篤敬及御史魏雲中等連章論列。

translations.literal: Zhenji, Juxiang, Dujing, and Censor Wei Yunzhong and others submitted linked memorials setting forth the case.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenji, Juxiang, Dujing, Censor Wei Yunzhong, and others filed a barrage of linked memorials pressing the case.

sentences.zh: 給事中商周祚亦敬同鄉，議並罪道南。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Shang Zhouzuo was also Jing's fellow townsman and recommended that Daonan be punished as well.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Shang Zhouzuo, another of Jing's fellow townsmen, recommended that Daonan be punished as well.

sentences.zh: 孟禎以道南發奸，不當罪，再疏糾駁。

translations.literal: Mengzhen argued that Daonan had exposed the wrongdoing and ought not be punished, and submitted another memorial to rebut it.
translations.idiomatic: Mengzhen argued that Daonan had exposed the fraud and should not be punished, and filed another memorial to rebut the charge.

sentences.zh: 帝竟如廷元等言，敕部更核。

translations.literal: The emperor finally followed Tingyuan and the rest, ordering the ministry to review the matter again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor finally sided with Tingyuan and his allies and ordered the ministry to review the case again.

sentences.zh: 廷元黨亓詩教遂劾正春首鼠兩端，正春尋引去。

translations.literal: Tingyuan's ally Qi Shijiao then impeached Zhengchun for vacillating; Zhengchun soon withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyuan's ally Qi Shijiao then impeached Zhengchun for vacillation, and Zhengchun soon resigned.

sentences.zh: 會熊廷弼之議亦起。

translations.literal: At the same time the controversy over Xiong Tingbi also arose.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time the controversy over Xiong Tingbi also erupted.

sentences.zh: 初，賓尹家居，嘗奪生員施天德妻為妾，不從，投繯死。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Binyin was living at home, he once seized the wife of the licentiate Shi Tiande to make her his concubine; she refused and hanged herself.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while living at home, Binyin had seized the wife of licentiate Shi Tiande to make her his concubine; when she refused, she hanged herself.

sentences.zh: 諸生馮應祥、芮永縉輩訟於官，為建祠，賓尹恥之。

translations.literal: The students Feng Yingxiang, Rui Yongjin, and their like sued at court and built a shrine for her; Binyin was shamed by it.
translations.idiomatic: Students Feng Yingxiang, Rui Yongjin, and others sued in court and built a shrine in her honor; Binyin was shamed by it.

sentences.zh: 後永縉又發諸生梅振祚、宣祚朋淫狀。

translations.literal: Later Yongjin also exposed the licentious companionship of the students Mei Zhenzuo and Xuan Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yongjin also exposed licentious conduct among the students Mei Zhenzuo and Xuan Zuo.

sentences.zh: 督學御史熊廷弼素交歡賓尹，判牒言此施、湯故智，欲藉雪賓尹前恥。

translations.literal: Education-intendant Censor Xiong Tingbi had long been on friendly terms with Binyin; in a judgment he said this was the old trick of Shi and Tang, intending to use it to wipe away Binyin's earlier shame.
translations.idiomatic: Education-intendant Censor Xiong Tingbi had long been on friendly terms with Binyin; in a judgment he called this the old trick of Shi and Tang, plainly seeking to erase Binyin's earlier disgrace.

sentences.zh: 又以所司報永縉及應祥行劣，杖殺永縉。

translations.literal: He also had the responsible office report Yongjin and Yingxiang for bad conduct and had Yongjin beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: He also had the responsible office report Yongjin and Yingxiang for misconduct and had Yongjin beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史荊養喬遂劾廷弼殺人媚人，疏上，徑自引歸。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Jing Yangqiao then impeached Tingbi for killing a man to please another; when the memorial went up, he withdrew directly and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Jing Yangqiao then impeached Tingbi for killing a man to curry favor; after submitting the memorial he withdrew from office and returned home.

sentences.zh: 廷弼亦疏辨。

translations.literal: Tingbi also submitted a memorial in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: Tingbi also submitted a memorial in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 都御史孫瑋議鐫養喬秩，令廷弼解職候勘。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Sun Wei recommended reducing Yangqiao's rank and ordering Tingbi relieved of office pending investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Sun Wei recommended demoting Yangqiao and suspending Tingbi pending investigation.

sentences.zh: 時南北臺諫議論方囂，各自所左右。

translations.literal: At the time debate among remonstrance officials north and south was clamorous, each side supporting its own men.
translations.idiomatic: At the time remonstrance officials north and south were shouting one another down, each faction backing its own men.

sentences.zh: 振基、孟禎、雲中策及給事李成名、麻僖、陳伯友，御史李邦華、崔爾進、李若星、潘之祥、翟鳳翀、徐良彥等持勘議甚力。

translations.literal: Zhenji, Mengzhen, Yunzhong, Ce, and Supervising Secretaries Li Chengming, Ma Xi, and Chen Boyou, and Censors Li Banghua, Cui Erjin, Li Ruoxing, Pan Zhixiang, Zhai Fengchong, and Xu Liangyan strongly upheld the investigation recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenji, Mengzhen, Wei Yunzhong, Liu Ce, and Supervising Secretaries Li Chengming, Ma Xi, and Chen Boyou, together with Censors Li Banghua, Cui Erjin, Li Ruoxing, Pan Zhixiang, Zhai Fengchong, and Xu Liangyan, strongly upheld the call for investigation.

sentences.zh: 而篤敬及給事中官應震、姜性、吳亮嗣、梅之煥、亓詩教、趙興邦，御史黃彥士，南京御史周遠等駁之，疏凡數十上。

translations.literal: But Dujing and Supervising Secretaries Guan Yingzhen, Jiang Xing, Wu Liangsi, Mei Zhihuan, Qi Shijiao, and Zhao Xingbang, Censor Huang Yanshi, and Nanjing Censor Zhou Yuan and others rebutted them; memorials numbering several tens were submitted.
translations.idiomatic: But Dujing, Supervising Secretaries Guan Yingzhen, Jiang Xing, Wu Liangsi, Mei Zhihuan, Qi Shijiao, and Zhao Xingbang, Censor Huang Yanshi, Nanjing Censor Zhou Yuan, and others rebutted them in dozens of memorials.

sentences.zh: 振基及諸給事御史復極言廷弼當勘，斥應震等黨庇，自是黨廷弼者頗屈。

translations.literal: Zhenji and the various supervising secretaries and censors again spoke forcefully that Tingbi ought to be investigated, denouncing Yingzhen and the rest for factional shielding; from then on those who sided with Tingbi were rather subdued.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenji and the other remonstrance officials again insisted that Tingbi must face investigation and denounced Yingzhen and his allies for partisan shielding; from then on Tingbi's faction was largely on the defensive.

sentences.zh: 帝竟納瑋言，今廷弼解職。

translations.literal: The emperor finally accepted Wei's view and had Tingbi relieved of office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor finally accepted Sun Wei's recommendation and had Xiong Tingbi relieved of office.

sentences.zh: 其黨大恨。

translations.literal: His faction hated this greatly.
translations.idiomatic: His faction hated it bitterly.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書趙煥者，惟詩教言是聽，乃以年例出振基及雲中、時熙於外。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Zhao Huan listened only to what Shijiao said; he then used the annual rotation rule to send Zhenji, Yunzhong, and Shixi outside the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Zhao Huan listened only to Qi Shijiao; he then used the annual rotation rule to post Zhenji, Wei Yunzhong, and Wang Shixi outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 振基得山東僉事，瑋亦引去。

translations.literal: Zhenji received the post of Shandong intendant; Wei also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenji was posted as intendant in Shandong, and Sun Wei resigned as well.

sentences.zh: 振基勁直敢言。

translations.literal: Zhenji was forceful, upright, and bold in speech.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenji was forceful, upright, and outspoken.

sentences.zh: 居諫垣僅半歲，數有建白。

translations.literal: He served in the remonstrance offices only half a year, yet repeatedly offered constructive proposals.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the remonstrance offices barely half a year, yet repeatedly offered constructive proposals.

sentences.zh: 既去，科場議猶未定，策復上疏極論。

translations.literal: After he departed, the examination controversy was still unsettled; Ce again submitted a forceful memorial.
translations.idiomatic: After he left, the examination controversy remained unsettled, and Liu Ce submitted another forceful memorial.

sentences.zh: 而賓尹黨必欲十七人並罪，以寬敬。

translations.literal: But Binyin's faction insisted that all seventeen men be punished together in order to leniently treat Jing.
translations.idiomatic: But Binyin's faction insisted that all seventeen men be punished together so as to soften the sentence for Jing.

sentences.zh: 孫慎行代正春，復集廷臣議。

translations.literal: Sun Shenxing replaced Zhengchun and again convened the court officials to discuss the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Shenxing replaced Zhengchun and again convened the court to discuss the case.

sentences.zh: 仍坐敬關節，而為十七人昭雪。

translations.literal: They still punished Jing for exam fraud, yet cleared the seventeen men.
translations.idiomatic: They still found Jing guilty of exam fraud, yet cleared the seventeen men.

sentences.zh: 疏竟留中。

translations.literal: The memorial was finally kept within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was shelved in the palace and never acted upon.

sentences.zh: 賓尹、敬有奧援，外廷又多助之，故議久不決。

translations.literal: Binyin and Jing had hidden support, and many in the outer court also helped them, so deliberation long went unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Binyin and Jing enjoyed hidden backing, and many officials in the outer court aided them as well, so the case dragged on unresolved.

sentences.zh: 篤敬復上疏論敬，陰詆諸黨人。

translations.literal: Dujing again submitted a memorial discussing Jing, covertly reviling the various faction members.
translations.idiomatic: Dujing again memorialized against Jing, covertly denouncing the faction members.

sentences.zh: 諸黨人旋出之外，並逐慎行。

translations.literal: The faction members were soon sent outside the capital, and Shenxing was driven out as well.
translations.idiomatic: The faction members were soon posted outside the capital, and Shenxing was driven out as well.

sentences.zh: 既而居相、策引去，之祥外遷。

translations.literal: Soon Juxiang and Ce withdrew, and Zhixiang was transferred outside.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Juxiang and Ce resigned, and Zhixiang was transferred out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 孟禎不平，疏言：「廷弼聽勘一事，業逐去一總憲，外轉兩言官矣，獨介介於之祥。

translations.literal: Mengzhen was indignant and memorialized: 'In the matter of Tingbi awaiting investigation, a censor-in-chief has already been driven out and two remonstrance officials transferred outside, yet they fixate only on Zhixiang.
translations.idiomatic: Indignant, Mengzhen memorialized: 'In the Tingbi investigation affair, a censor-in-chief has already been removed and two remonstrance officials transferred out—yet they fixate only on Zhixiang.

sentences.zh: 敬科場一案，亦去兩侍郎、兩言官矣，復斷斷於篤敬，毋乃已甚乎！」

translations.literal: In Jing's examination case, two vice ministers and two remonstrance officials have already been removed, yet they persistently fixate on Dujing—is this not excessive!'
translations.idiomatic: In Han Jing's examination scandal, two vice ministers and two remonstrance officials have already been removed, yet they persistently target Dujing—is this not going too far!'

sentences.zh: 孟禎遂亦調外。

translations.literal: Mengzhen was then also transferred outside.
translations.idiomatic: Mengzhen was then transferred out of the capital as well.

sentences.zh: 凡與敬為難者，朝無一人。

translations.literal: Of all who had opposed Jing, not one remained at court.
translations.idiomatic: Not a single man who had opposed Han Jing remained at court.

sentences.zh: 敬由是得寬典，僅謫行人司副。

translations.literal: Jing thereby received lenient treatment and was merely demoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jing thereby escaped with a light sentence, demoted only to vice director of the Court of Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 蓋七年而事始竣雲。

translations.literal: Covering seven years, the affair was only then concluded.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years passed before the affair was finally laid to rest.

sentences.zh: 振基到官，尋以憂去，卒於家。

translations.literal: When Zhenji reached his post, he soon left on mourning and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhenji took up his post, he soon left on mourning obligations and died at home.

sentences.zh: 子必顯，字克孝。

translations.literal: Zi Bixian, styled Kexiao.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Bixian, styled Kexiao.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十四年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-fourth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-fourth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 官文選員外郎，為尚書趙南星所重。

translations.literal: He served as vice director in the Selection Office and was highly regarded by Minister Zhao Nanxing.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice director in the Selection Office and was highly regarded by Minister Zhao Nanxing.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年冬，魏忠賢羅織清流，御史陳睿謨劾其世投門戶，遂削籍。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fifth year of Tianqi, Wei Zhongxian fabricated charges against the upright faction; Censor Chen Ruimo impeached him for generations of factional allegiance, and he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fifth year of Tianqi, as Wei Zhongxian fabricated charges against the upright faction, Censor Chen Ruimo impeached him for generations of factional allegiance, and he was removed from the official rolls.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年，起驗封郎中，移考功。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen, he was reappointed as Director in the Seal Verification Bureau and transferred to the Bureau of Evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Chongzhen reign, he was recalled to serve as director in the Seal Verification Bureau, then transferred to the Bureau of Evaluations.

sentences.zh: 明年，移文選。

translations.literal: The next year, he was transferred to the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 尚書王永光雅不喜東林，給事中常自裕因劾其推舉不當數事，且詆以貪汙。

translations.literal: Minister Wang Yongguang had long disliked the Donglin faction; Supervising Secretary Chang Ziyu impeached him on several counts of improper nominations and also slandered him for corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Yongguang had always disliked the Donglin faction. Supervising Secretary Chang Ziyu impeached him for several improper appointments and accused him of corruption as well.

sentences.zh: 御史吳履中又劾其紊亂選法。

translations.literal: Censor Wu Lüzhong also impeached him for throwing the selection regulations into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wu Lüzhong also impeached him for muddling the appointment regulations.

sentences.zh: 必顯兩疏辨，帝不聽，謫山西按察司經歷，量移南京禮部主事。

translations.literal: Bixian submitted two memorials in his defense, but the emperor would not listen; he was demoted to Administrative Assistant in the Shanxi Surveillance Commission and then, by discretionary transfer, made Chief Clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Bixian submitted two memorials in his defense, but the emperor would not heed them. He was demoted to administrative assistant in the Shanxi Surveillance Commission, then later reassigned by discretionary transfer to chief clerk in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 道出柘城、歸德，適流賊來犯，皆為設守，完其城。

translations.literal: On the road he passed through Zhecheng and Guide; just as bandit armies were attacking, he set up defenses for both and preserved their city walls intact.
translations.idiomatic: Traveling through Zhecheng and Guide, he found both cities under attack by roving bandits. He organized defenses at each place and kept their walls intact.

sentences.zh: 一時推知兵。

translations.literal: For a time he was acclaimed as knowledgeable in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: For a time he was widely praised for his knowledge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 歷尚寶司丞、大理左寺丞。

translations.literal: He successively served as Vice Director of the Seal Keeper's Office and as Vice Director of the Left Branch of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as vice director of the Seal Keeper's Office and vice director of the left branch of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 十一年冬，都城被兵，兵部兩侍郎皆缺，尚書楊嗣昌請不拘常格，博推才望者遷補，遂擢必顯右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year, the capital came under attack; both vice ministers of the Ministry of War were vacant. Minister Yang Sichang requested that the usual rules not be observed and that men of talent and reputation be broadly recommended for promotion and filling vacancies, whereupon Bixian was promoted to Right Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the eleventh year, as the capital came under attack, both vice ministers of the Ministry of War were vacant. Minister Yang Sichang asked that normal procedures be set aside and men of talent and reputation be broadly considered for appointment, and Bixian was promoted to right vice minister.

sentences.zh: 甫一月，無疾而卒。

translations.literal: Barely a month later, he died without illness.
translations.idiomatic: Barely a month later, he died suddenly without known illness.

sentences.zh: 丁元薦，字長孺，長興人。

translations.literal: Ding Yuanjian, styled Changru, was a native of Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Yuanjian, styled Changru, was from Changxing.

sentences.zh: 父應詔，江西僉事。

translations.literal: His father Yingzhao was a Regional Inspector of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yingzhao served as regional inspector of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 元薦舉萬歷十四年進士。

translations.literal: Yuanjian passed the jinshi examination in the fourteenth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjian passed the jinshi examination in the fourteenth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 請告歸。

translations.literal: He requested leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He requested leave and returned home.

sentences.zh: 家居八年，始謁選為中書舍人。

translations.literal: He remained at home for eight years before presenting himself for appointment and receiving the post of Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: After eight years at home, he finally presented himself for office and was appointed secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 甫期月，上封事萬言，極陳時弊。

translations.literal: Barely a month later, he submitted a sealed memorial of ten thousand characters, exhaustively setting forth the evils of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Barely a month into his term, he submitted a sealed memorial ten thousand characters long, laying bare the evils of the age in exhaustive detail.

sentences.zh: 言今日事勢可寒心者三：饑民思亂也，武備積弛也，日本封貢也。

translations.literal: He said that three things in the present situation chilled the heart: starving people thinking of rebellion, military preparations long neglected, and Japan's tribute and trade missions.
translations.idiomatic: He named three aspects of the present situation that chilled the heart: starving people turning toward rebellion, military readiness long neglected, and relations with Japan over tribute and trade.

sentences.zh: 可浩嘆者七：征斂苛急也，賞罰不明也，忠賢廢錮也，輔臣妒嫉也，議論滋多也，士習敗壞也，褒功恤忠未備也。

translations.literal: Seven things worthy of deep lament: oppressive and urgent taxation, unclear rewards and punishments, loyal and worthy men imprisoned, grand secretaries jealous and envious, ever more factional wrangling, scholar-official habits corrupted, and insufficient honoring of merit and care for the loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Seven things worthy of deep lament: oppressive taxation, unclear rewards and punishments, imprisonment of loyal and worthy men, jealousy among grand secretaries, ever multiplying factional wrangling, corruption of scholar-official conduct, and failure to honor merit and care for the loyal.

sentences.zh: 坐視而不可救藥者二，則紀綱、人心也。

translations.literal: Two things that one watches idly and yet cannot remedy are the basic order and the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Two evils that could only be watched idly, yet seemed beyond remedy, were the breakdown of basic order and the loss of the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 其所言輔臣，專斥首輔王錫爵，元薦座主也。

translations.literal: The grand secretary he attacked was none other than Chief Grand Secretary Wang Xijue, Yuanjian's own former examiner.
translations.idiomatic: The grand secretary he singled out for attack was Chief Grand Secretary Wang Xijue—Yuanjian's own former examiner.

sentences.zh: 二十七年京察。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year came the capital performance review.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year the capital performance review was held.

sentences.zh: 元薦家居，坐浮躁論調。

translations.literal: Yuanjian was at home; he was judged as frivolous and argumentative.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjian was at home at the time and was judged frivolous and contentious.

sentences.zh: 閱十有二年，起廣東按察司經歷，移禮部主事。

translations.literal: After twelve years had passed, he was reappointed Administrative Assistant in the Guangdong Surveillance Commission and transferred to Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve years later he was recalled as administrative assistant in the Guangdong Surveillance Commission, then transferred to chief clerk in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 甫抵官，值京察事竣，尚書孫丕揚力清邪黨，反為其黨所攻。

translations.literal: Barely after he reached his post, the capital review was concluding; Minister Sun Piyang strove to purge the evil faction but was in turn attacked by that faction.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had he reached his post when the capital review concluded. Minister Sun Piyang strove to purge the corrupt faction, only to be attacked by that very faction.

sentences.zh: 副都御史許弘綱故共掌察，見群小橫甚，畏之，累疏請竣察典，語頗示異。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Xu Honggang had formerly shared supervision of the review; seeing how wildly the petty men behaved, he feared them and repeatedly submitted memorials asking that the review be concluded, his language showing clear dissent.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Xu Honggang had originally shared supervision of the review. Seeing how brazen the petty faction had become, he was afraid and repeatedly submitted memorials asking that the review be brought to a close—language that plainly signaled his dissent.

sentences.zh: 群小藉以攻丕揚。

translations.literal: The petty men seized on this to attack Piyang.
translations.idiomatic: The petty faction seized on this to attack Sun Piyang.

sentences.zh: 察疏猶未下，人情杌隉，慮事中變，然無敢言者。

translations.literal: The review memorial had not yet been issued; public sentiment was unsettled, and people feared something might change midway, yet no one dared speak out.
translations.idiomatic: The review report had not yet been issued. Public sentiment was unsettled, and many feared the outcome might yet change—but no one dared speak up.

sentences.zh: 元薦乃上言弘綱持議不宜前卻，並盡發諸人隱狀。

translations.literal: Yuanjian then submitted a memorial saying that Honggang's holding to his position should not waver back and forth, and fully exposed the hidden conduct of the various men.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjian then submitted a memorial arguing that Xu Honggang should not vacillate on his position, and fully exposed the hidden misconduct of those involved.

sentences.zh: 黨人惡之，交章論劾無虛日。

translations.literal: The faction hated him; memorials impeaching him poured in day after day without cease.
translations.idiomatic: The faction hated him, and impeachment memorials poured in day after day without cease.

sentences.zh: 元薦復再疏辨晰，竟不安其身而去。

translations.literal: Yuanjian again submitted two clarifying memorials in his defense, but in the end could not secure his position and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjian submitted two more memorials clarifying his position, but in the end could not remain at his post and left.

sentences.zh: 其後邪黨愈熾，正人屏斥殆盡，至有以「《六經》亂天下」語入鄉試策問者。

translations.literal: After this the evil faction grew still stronger, upright men were driven out almost entirely, and there were even provincial examination policy questions using the phrase "The Six Classics disorder the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the corrupt faction grew ever stronger, upright men were driven out almost entirely, and there were even provincial examination policy questions framed around the phrase "The Six Classics disorder the realm."

sentences.zh: 元薦家居不勝憤，復馳疏闕下，極詆亂政之叛高皇、邪說之叛孔子者。

translations.literal: Yuanjian, unable to contain his anger while at home, again rushed a memorial to the palace gate, fiercely denouncing corrupt government as rebellion against the Hongwu Emperor and perverse doctrines as rebellion against Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to contain his anger at home, Yuanjian rushed another memorial to the palace gate, fiercely denouncing corrupt government as treason against the Hongwu Emperor and heterodox doctrines as treason against Confucius.

sentences.zh: 疏雖不報，黨人益惡之。

translations.literal: Though the memorial received no response, the faction hated him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Though the memorial went unanswered, the faction hated him all the more.

sentences.zh: 四十五年京察，遂復以不謹削籍。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year capital review, he was again removed from the rolls for lack of prudent conduct.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital review of the forty-fifth year, he was again struck from the rolls for lack of prudent conduct.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，大起遺佚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi, the court broadly recalled men who had been passed over.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, the court broadly recalled men who had long been passed over.

sentences.zh: 元薦格於例，獨不召。

translations.literal: Yuanjian was blocked by precedent and alone was not summoned.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjian alone was not summoned, barred by precedent.

sentences.zh: 至四年，廷臣交訟其冤，起刑部檢校，歷尚寶少卿。

translations.literal: By the fourth year, court officials together argued over his wrongful treatment; he was appointed Proofreader in the Ministry of Punishments and rose to Vice Director of the Seal Keeper's Office.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth year court officials had repeatedly argued that he had been wronged. He was appointed proofreader in the Ministry of Punishments and eventually rose to vice director of the Seal Keeper's Office.

sentences.zh: 明年，朝事大變，復削其籍。

translations.literal: The next year court affairs changed greatly, and he was again struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The following year court affairs changed dramatically, and he was again removed from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 元薦初學於許孚遠，已，從顧憲成遊。

translations.literal: Yuanjian first studied under Xu Fuyuan; afterward he associated with Gu Xiancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjian first studied under Xu Fuyuan, then became a follower of Gu Xiancheng.

sentences.zh: 慷慨負氣，遇事奮前，屢躓無少挫。

translations.literal: Bold and proud in spirit, he charged forward when affairs arose; though he stumbled again and again, he was scarcely diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and proud in spirit, he charged ahead whenever a cause arose. Though he stumbled again and again, he was never much deterred.

sentences.zh: 通籍四十年，前後服官不滿一載。

translations.literal: For forty years he was on the rolls, yet in all he served in office for less than one year.
translations.idiomatic: Though on the rolls for forty years, he held office for less than a year in total.

sentences.zh: 同郡沈淮召入閣，邀一見，謝不往。

translations.literal: Shen Huai of the same prefecture was summoned into the Grand Secretariat and invited him to a meeting; he declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Huai of the same prefecture was summoned into the Grand Secretariat and invited him to meet, but he declined to go.

sentences.zh: 嘗過高攀龍，請與交歡，辭曰：「吾老矣，不能涉嫌要津。」

translations.literal: Once, passing by Gao Panlong, Gao asked to join in friendly relations; he declined, saying, "I am old and cannot court suspicion at a critical post."
translations.idiomatic: Once, visiting Gao Panlong, Gao asked to befriend him. He declined, saying, "I am old and cannot court suspicion by associating with men at critical posts."

sentences.zh: 遽別去。

translations.literal: He immediately took his leave and departed.
translations.idiomatic: With that he immediately took his leave and departed.

sentences.zh: 當東林、浙黨之分，浙黨所彈射東林者，李三才之次，則元薦與於玉立。

translations.literal: When the Donglin and Zhejiang factions were divided, after Li Sancai those whom the Zhejiang faction attacked among the Donglin were Yuanjian and Yu Yuli.
translations.idiomatic: When the Donglin and Zhejiang factions were at odds, after Li Sancai the Donglin men most targeted by the Zhejiang faction were Yuanjian and Yu Yuli.

sentences.zh: 玉立，字中甫，金壇人。

translations.literal: Yuli, styled Zhongfu, was a native of Jintan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yuli, styled Zhongfu, was from Jintan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十一年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 除刑部主事，進員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Punishments and promoted to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief clerk in the Ministry of Punishments and promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 二十年七月，疏陳時政闕失，言：「陛下寵幸貴妃，宴逸無度。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twentieth year, he submitted a memorial laying out the failings of current policy, saying, "Your Majesty dotes on the Noble Consort and feasts in pleasure without limit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the twentieth year he submitted a memorial laying out the failings of current policy, saying, "Your Majesty dotes on the Noble Consort and indulges in feasting and leisure without limit.

sentences.zh: 恣行威怒，鞭笞群下，宮人奄豎無辜死者千人。

translations.literal: You wield anger at will and lash your subordinates; among palace women and eunuchs, a thousand innocents have died.
translations.idiomatic: You unleash your wrath at will and lash your subordinates; among palace women and eunuchs, a thousand innocents have died.

sentences.zh: 夫人懷必死之心，而使處肘腋房闥間，倘因利乘便，甘心一逞，可不寒心！

translations.literal: When people harbor minds resolved on death yet are made to dwell within your very armpits and inner chambers, should they seize an opportune moment to satisfy themselves in one stroke, would that not chill the heart!
translations.idiomatic: When people carry death in their hearts yet are kept at your very side, within arm's reach in the inner chambers, should they seize a moment of opportunity to vent their grievance, would that not chill the heart!

sentences.zh: 田義本一奸豎，陛下寵信不疑。

translations.literal: Tian Yi was originally a treacherous eunuch, yet Your Majesty favors and trusts him without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yi was originally a treacherous eunuch, yet Your Majesty favors and trusts him without reservation.

sentences.zh: 邇者奏牘或下或留，推舉或用或否，道路籍籍，鹹謂義簸弄其間。

translations.literal: Recently memorials have sometimes been issued and sometimes held back, recommendations sometimes accepted and sometimes rejected; rumors fill the roads, and all say Yi is manipulating matters between them.
translations.idiomatic: Recently memorials have sometimes been issued and sometimes held back, recommendations sometimes accepted and sometimes rejected. Rumors fill the roads, and all say Tian Yi is manipulating affairs behind the scenes.

sentences.zh: 蓋義以陛下為城社，而外廷之憸邪又以義為城社。

translations.literal: For Yi takes Your Majesty as his rampart and altar, and the sycophants of the outer court in turn take Yi as their rampart and altar.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yi uses Your Majesty as his shield, and the sycophants of the outer court in turn use Tian Yi as theirs.

sentences.zh: 黨合謀連，其禍難量。

translations.literal: Factions join and conspiracies link; the disaster is hard to measure.
translations.idiomatic: Factions unite and conspiracies multiply—the disaster they portend is incalculable.

sentences.zh: 且陛下一惑於嬖幸，而數年以來，問安視膳，郊廟朝講，一切不行。

translations.literal: Moreover, since Your Majesty was once bemused by favorites, for several years now greetings to the empress dowager, attendance at meals, suburban sacrifices, ancestral temple rites, court audiences, and lectures—all have gone unperformed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, ever since Your Majesty fell under the spell of favorites, for several years now visits to the empress dowager, attendance at meals, suburban sacrifices, ancestral rites, court audiences, and lectures have all been neglected.

sentences.zh: 至邊烽四起，禍亂成形，猶不足以動憂危之情，奪晏安之習。

translations.literal: Even when frontier beacons blaze on every side and disaster and rebellion take shape, this is still not enough to stir feelings of anxiety and peril or break the habit of ease and comfort.
translations.idiomatic: Even when frontier beacons blaze on every side and disaster and rebellion take shape, this still does not stir feelings of anxiety and peril or break the habit of ease and comfort.

sentences.zh: 是君身之不修，未有甚於今日者矣。

translations.literal: Never has failure to cultivate one's person as ruler been more extreme than today.
translations.idiomatic: Never has a ruler's neglect of self-cultivation been more extreme than it is today.

sentences.zh: 夫宮庭震驚，而陛下若罔聞，何以解兩宮之憂？

translations.literal: When the palace is shaken with alarm and Your Majesty acts as though you heard nothing, how can you dispel the worries of the two palaces?
translations.idiomatic: When the palace is shaken with alarm and Your Majesty acts as though you heard nothing, how can you ease the worries of the empress dowagers?

sentences.zh: 深拱禁中，開夤緣之隙，致邪孽侵權，而陛下未察其奸，何以杜旁落之漸？

translations.literal: You sit deeply withdrawn within the Forbidden City, opening gaps for opportunists, allowing evil minions to encroach on power, yet Your Majesty has not detected their treachery—how can you check the gradual erosion of authority?
translations.idiomatic: Deeply withdrawn within the Forbidden City, you open gaps for opportunists and allow evil minions to encroach on power—yet fail to detect their treachery. How can you check the gradual erosion of imperial authority?

sentences.zh: 萬國欽輩未嘗忤主，而終於禁錮，何以勵骨鯁之臣？

translations.literal: Men like Wan Guoqin never offended the ruler yet ended in imprisonment—how can you encourage blunt and upright ministers?
translations.idiomatic: Men like Wan Guoqin never offended the throne yet ended in imprisonment—how can you encourage blunt and upright ministers?

sentences.zh: 上下隔越，國議、軍機無由參斷，而陛下稱旨下令，終不出閨闥之間，何以盡大臣之謀？

translations.literal: Upper and lower are separated; state deliberations and military affairs cannot be jointly decided, yet orders that accord with Your Majesty's wishes ultimately issue only from the inner apartments—how can you exhaust the counsel of your grand ministers?
translations.idiomatic: Court and throne are estranged; state policy and military affairs cannot be jointly decided, yet orders that accord with your wishes issue only from the inner apartments—how can you draw on the full counsel of your grand ministers?

sentences.zh: 忠良多擯，邪佞得名，何以作群臣之氣？

translations.literal: Many loyal men are cast aside while evil flatterers win reputation—how can you rouse the spirit of the officials?
translations.idiomatic: Loyal men are cast aside while evil flatterers win renown—how can you raise the morale of the officials?

sentences.zh: 遠近之民，皆疑至尊日求般樂，不顧百姓塗炭，何以系天下之心？」

translations.literal: People near and far all suspect that the Son of Heaven daily seeks varied pleasures and pays no heed to the people's torment—how can you bind the hearts of the realm?"
translations.idiomatic: People near and far suspect that the Son of Heaven seeks only varied pleasures each day and pays no heed to the people's suffering—how can you hold the hearts of the realm?"

sentences.zh: 因力言李如松、麻貴不可為大將，鄭洛不當再起，石星不堪為本兵。

translations.literal: He then forcefully argued that Li Rusong and Ma Gui were unfit to serve as grand generals, that Zheng Luo should not be restored to office, and that Shi Xing was unfit to serve as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He then forcefully argued that Li Rusong and Ma Gui were unfit to serve as grand generals, that Zheng Luo should not be restored to office, and that Shi Xing was unfit to serve as minister of war.

sentences.zh: 疏入，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but received no response.

sentences.zh: 尋進郎中，謝病歸。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Director and returned home on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to director and retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 久之，起故官。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was restored to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was restored to his former office.

sentences.zh: 康丕揚輩欲以妖書陷郭正域，玉立獨左右之。

translations.literal: Kang Piyang and his faction wished to entrap Guo Zhengyu with the demonic book affair; Yuli alone supported him on both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Piyang and his faction tried to entrap Guo Zhengyu with the demonic book affair; Yuli alone stood by him.

sentences.zh: 會有言醫人沈令譽實為妖書者，搜其篋，得玉立與吏部郎中王士騏書，中及其起官事。

translations.literal: Just then someone said the physician Shen Lingyu was in fact author of the demonic book; searching his case, they found letters between Yuli and Wang Shiqi, Director in the Ministry of Personnel, mentioning his restoration to office.
translations.idiomatic: Just then someone claimed that the physician Shen Lingyu was the true author of the demonic book. Searching his case, investigators found letters between Yuli and Wang Shiqi of the Ministry of Personnel that touched on Yuli's restoration to office.

sentences.zh: 帝方下吏部按問，而玉立遽疏辨。

translations.literal: The emperor had just ordered the Ministry of Personnel to investigate, when Yuli hastily submitted a memorial in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had just ordered the Ministry of Personnel to investigate when Yuli hastily submitted a memorial in his defense.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，褫其官。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and stripped him of his office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and stripped him of his office.

sentences.zh: 玉立倜儻好事。

translations.literal: Yuli was unconventional and fond of engaging in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yuli was unconventional and always ready to take up a cause.

sentences.zh: 海內建言廢錮諸臣，鹹以東林為歸。

translations.literal: Throughout the realm, officials who had memorialized and been imprisoned all looked to the Donglin as their refuge.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the realm, memorializing officials who had been imprisoned all looked to the Donglin faction as their rallying point.

sentences.zh: 玉立與通聲氣，東林名益盛。

translations.literal: Yuli communicated with them in mutual understanding, and the Donglin name grew ever more eminent.
translations.idiomatic: Yuli maintained contact with them, and the Donglin name grew ever more eminent.

sentences.zh: 而攻東林者，率謂玉立遙制朝權，以是詬病東林。

translations.literal: But those who attacked the Donglin generally said Yuli remotely controlled court power, and on this ground slandered the Donglin.
translations.idiomatic: But those who attacked the Donglin generally claimed that Yuli remotely controlled court power—and on that basis smeared the Donglin faction.

sentences.zh: 玉立居家久之，數被推薦。

translations.literal: Yuli remained at home for a long time and was repeatedly recommended.
translations.idiomatic: Yuli lived at home for a long time and was repeatedly recommended for office.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，稍起光祿丞，辭不赴。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he was slightly raised to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; he declined and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he was offered appointment as vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; he declined to take it up.

sentences.zh: 言者猶齮龁不已，御史馬孟禎抗章直之，帝皆不省。

translations.literal: Critics still gnawed at him without end; Censor Ma Mengzhen submitted a forceful memorial in his defense, but the emperor paid no heed to any of it.
translations.idiomatic: His critics still attacked him relentlessly. Censor Ma Mengzhen submitted a forceful memorial in his defense, but the emperor paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 又三年，以光祿少卿召，終不出。

translations.literal: Three years later he was summoned as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments but in the end never emerged.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was summoned as vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, but he never emerged from retirement.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，錄先朝罪譴諸臣，玉立已前卒，贈尚寶卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi, when the court recorded men punished in the previous reign, Yuli had already died earlier; he was posthumously granted the title Director of the Seal Keeper's Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, when the court posthumously honored men punished in the previous reign, Yuli had already died. He was granted the posthumous title of director of the Seal Keeper's Office.

sentences.zh: 李樸，字繼白，朝邑人。

translations.literal: Li Pu, styled Jibai, was a native of Chaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Pu, styled Jibai, was from Chaoyi.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十九年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-ninth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-ninth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 由彰德推官入為戶部主事。

translations.literal: From the post of magistrate's aide in Zhangde he entered office as Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as chief clerk in the Ministry of Revenue after serving as magistrate's aide in Zhangde.

sentences.zh: 四十年夏，樸以朝多朋黨，清流廢錮，疏請破奸黨，錄遺賢，因為顧憲成、於玉立、李三才、孫丕揚辨謗，而薦呂坤、姜士昌、鄒元標、趙南星。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fortieth year, Pu, seeing that the court abounded in factions and that upright officials were imprisoned, submitted a memorial requesting the breaking of evil factions and the recording of overlooked talent; he thereby cleared slander against Gu Xiancheng, Yu Yuli, Li Sancai, and Sun Piyang, and recommended Lü Kun, Jiang Shichang, Zou Yuanbiao, and Zhao Nanxing.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fortieth year, seeing the court riddled with factions and upright officials imprisoned, Pu submitted a memorial asking that corrupt factions be broken up and overlooked talent restored. He cleared slander against Gu Xiancheng, Yu Yuli, Li Sancai, and Sun Piyang, and recommended Lü Kun, Jiang Shichang, Zou Yuanbiao, and Zhao Nanxing.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed it.

sentences.zh: 明年，再遷郎中。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred again to Director.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted again to director.

sentences.zh: 齊、楚、浙三黨勢盛，稍持議論者，群噪逐之。

translations.literal: The three factions of Qi, Chu, and Zhe were powerful; anyone who held even slightly to independent opinion was hounded out by clamoring mobs.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi, Chu, and Zhe factions were ascendant; anyone who ventured even a slightly independent opinion was hounded out by clamoring mobs.

sentences.zh: 主事沈正宗、賀烺皆與相拄，坐貶官。

translations.literal: Chief Clerks Shen Zhengzong and He Lang both opposed them and were demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerks Shen Zhengzong and He Lang both stood against them and were demoted.

sentences.zh: 樸性戇，積憤不平。

translations.literal: Pu was blunt by nature and nursed accumulated anger and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Blunt by nature, Pu nursed a growing sense of injustice.

sentences.zh: 其年十二月，上疏曰：

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of that year, he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of that year he submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 朝廷設言官，假之權勢，本責以糾正諸司，舉刺非法，非欲其結黨逞威，挾制百僚，排斥端人正士也。

translations.literal: The court establishes remonstrating officials and lends them power and authority, originally charging them to correct the various offices and expose illegal conduct—not wishing them to form factions and flaunt power, coerce the hundred officials, and drive out upright and proper men.
translations.idiomatic: The court establishes remonstrating officials and grants them power and authority, charging them to correct the various offices and expose wrongdoing—not to form factions, flaunt their power, coerce fellow officials, and drive out upright men.

sentences.zh: 今乃深結戚畹近坐，威制大僚；

translations.literal: Now they form deep ties with consort kin and those close to the throne, and overpower grand officials;
translations.idiomatic: Now they form deep ties with consort kin and those close to the throne, and bully grand officials;

sentences.zh: 日事請寄，廣納賂遺；

translations.literal: daily engage in entrustments and widely accept bribes;
translations.idiomatic: they daily accept entrustments and widely accept bribes;

sentences.zh: 褻衣小車，遨遊市肆，狎比娼優；

translations.literal: in plain clothes and small carriages they roam the markets, keeping intimate company with prostitutes and actors;
translations.idiomatic: dressed in plain clothes and riding in small carriages, they roam the markets and consort with prostitutes and actors;

sentences.zh: 或就飲商賈之家，流連山人之室。

translations.literal: sometimes drinking at merchants' houses, lingering in the dwellings of mountain hermits.
translations.idiomatic: sometimes drinking at merchants' homes, lingering in the dwellings of reclusive scholars.

sentences.zh: 身則鬼蜮，反誣他人。

translations.literal: They themselves are devils and serpents yet turn to slander others.
translations.idiomatic: They themselves are treacherous as devils and serpents, yet turn to slander others.

sentences.zh: 此蓋明欺至尊不覽章奏，大臣柔弱無為，故猖狂恣肆，至於此極。

translations.literal: This plainly takes advantage of the Son of Heaven's not reading memorials and the grand ministers' weakness and inaction, and so they run wild without restraint to this extreme.
translations.idiomatic: This plainly exploits the fact that the Son of Heaven does not read memorials and that grand ministers are weak and inactive, and so they run wild without restraint to this extreme.

sentences.zh: 臣謂此輩皆可斬也。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that this lot should all be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject holds that this lot should all be put to death.

sentences.zh: 孫瑋、湯兆京、李邦華、孫居相、周起元各爭職掌，則群攻之。

translations.literal: When Sun Wei, Tang Zhaojing, Li Banghua, Sun Juxiang, and Zhou Qiyuan each disputed their jurisdiction, the faction launched a collective attack on them.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Wei, Tang Zhaojing, Li Banghua, Sun Juxiang, and Zhou Qiyuan each disputed their jurisdictions, the faction attacked them collectively.

sentences.zh: 今或去或罰，惟存一居相，猶謂之黨。

translations.literal: Now some are removed or punished, and only one Juxiang remains, yet they still call it a faction.
translations.idiomatic: Some have already been removed or punished, and only Sun Juxiang remains—and still they call it a faction.

sentences.zh: 夫居相一人耳，何能為？

translations.literal: But Juxiang is only one man—what can he do?
translations.idiomatic: But Juxiang is only one man. What can he do alone?

sentences.zh: 彼浙江則姚宗文、劉廷元輩，湖廣則官應震、吳亮嗣、黃彥士輩，山東則亓詩教、周永春輩，四川則田一甲輩，百人合為一心，以擠排善類，而趙興邦輩附麗之。

translations.literal: In Zhejiang there are Yao Zongwen, Liu Tingyuan, and their like; in Huguang, Guan Yingzhen, Wu Liangsi, Huang Yanshi, and their like; in Shandong, Qi Shijiao, Zhou Yongchun, and their like; in Sichuan, Tian Yijia and his like—a hundred men united as one mind to squeeze out and drive away good men, with Zhao Xingbang and his kind attaching themselves to them.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhejiang there are Yao Zongwen, Liu Tingyuan, and their kind; in Huguang, Guan Yingzhen, Wu Liangsi, Huang Yanshi, and their kind; in Shandong, Qi Shijiao, Zhou Yongchun, and their kind; in Sichuan, Tian Yijia and his kind—a hundred men united in one purpose to squeeze out and destroy good officials, with Zhao Xingbang and his cohort attaching themselves to them.

sentences.zh: 陛下試思居相一人敵宗文輩百人，孰為有黨耶？

translations.literal: Your Majesty, consider: one Juxiang against a hundred of Zongwen's kind—who forms the faction?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, consider: one Juxiang against a hundred men like Zongwen—who really forms the faction?

sentences.zh: 乃攻東林者，今日指為亂政，明日目為擅權，不知東林居何官？

translations.literal: Those who attack the Donglin faction today call them disorderly in government, tomorrow accuse them of usurping power—yet what offices do the Donglin hold?
translations.idiomatic: Those who attack the Donglin today call them subversives; tomorrow they accuse them of usurping power. Yet what offices do the Donglin hold?

sentences.zh: 操何柄？

translations.literal: What authority do they wield?
translations.idiomatic: What power do they wield?

sentences.zh: 在朝列言路者，反謂無權，而林下投閑杜門樂道者，反謂有權，此不可欺三尺豎子，而乃以欺陛下哉！

translations.literal: Those in office holding positions on the remonstrance channel are said to have no power, while those retired under the Donglin trees, casting aside office and shutting their doors to pursue the Way, are said to have power—this cannot deceive a child three feet tall, yet they would use it to deceive Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: Officials in active remonstrance posts are said to have no power, while retired Donglin men who have shut their doors to pursue the Way are said to wield power. A child could see through this—yet they would use it to deceive Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 至若黃克纘贓私鉅萬，已敗猶見留；

translations.literal: As for Huang Kezuan, whose private graft ran to tens of thousands—though already exposed he is still retained;
translations.idiomatic: Huang Kezuan's private graft ran to tens of thousands—though already exposed, he is still retained;

sentences.zh: 顧憲成清風百代，已死猶被論；

translations.literal: Gu Xiancheng, whose integrity would shine for a hundred generations—though already dead he is still attacked;
translations.idiomatic: Gu Xiancheng, whose integrity would shine for a hundred generations—though already dead, he is still attacked;

sentences.zh: 而封疆坐死如陳用賓，科場作奸如韓敬，趨時鬻爵如趙煥，殺人媚人如熊廷弼，猶為之營護，為之稱冤。
