translations.literal: while Chen Yongbin, who died in office at the frontier, Han Jing, who committed fraud in the examination halls, Zhao Huan, who sold offices to suit the times, and Xiong Tingbi, who killed men to flatter others—all are still shielded for them and pleaded innocent on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: yet Chen Yongbin, who died at his frontier post; Han Jing, who rigged the examinations; Zhao Huan, who sold offices to suit the times; and Xiong Tingbi, who killed men to curry favor—all are still shielded and proclaimed innocent.

sentences.zh: 國典安在哉！

translations.literal: Where are the laws of the state!
translations.idiomatic: Where are the laws of the realm!

sentences.zh: 望俯察臣言，立賜威斷，先斬臣以謝諸奸，然後斬諸奸以謝天下，宗社幸甚。

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to examine my words closely and immediately grant resolute judgment: first execute me to answer to the various villains, then execute the various villains to answer to the realm—the altars of state would be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to examine my words and act decisively: first execute me to atone to the villains, then execute the villains to atone to the realm. The altars of state would be greatly blessed.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，臺諫皆大恨。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the censorate remonstrators all hated it deeply.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the censorate remonstrators were deeply resentful.

sentences.zh: 宗文等及其黨力詆，並侵居相，而一甲且羅織其贓私。

translations.literal: Zongwen and the others, with their faction, attacked it vehemently, also assailing Juxiang, while Yijia even fabricated charges of graft against him.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwen and his faction attacked it fiercely, also assailing Juxiang, while Yijia even fabricated charges of corruption against him.

sentences.zh: 帝雅不喜言官，得樸疏，心善之。

translations.literal: The emperor had never liked remonstrating officials, but receiving Pu's memorial, he was favorably disposed toward it in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had never liked remonstrating officials, but when he received Pu's memorial, he was favorably disposed toward it.

sentences.zh: 會大學士葉向高、方從哲亦謂樸言過當，乃下部院議罰。

translations.literal: But Grand Secretaries Ye Xianggao and Fang Congzhe also said Pu's words had gone too far, and so the matter was sent down to the ministries and courts to discuss punishment.
translations.idiomatic: But Grand Secretaries Ye Xianggao and Fang Congzhe also held that Pu's words had gone too far, and the matter was sent down to the ministries and courts to discuss punishment.

sentences.zh: 而樸再疏發亮嗣、應震、彥士、一甲贓私，及宗文、廷元庇韓敬、興邦媚趙煥狀，且言：「詩教為群兇盟主，實社稷巨蠹，陛下尤不可不察。」

translations.literal: But Pu submitted another memorial exposing the graft of Liangsi, Yingzhen, Yanshi, and Yijia, and the circumstances in which Zongwen and Tingyuan shielded Han Jing and Xingbang fawned on Zhao Huan, saying furthermore: "Shijiao is chieftain of the band of villains and is in truth a great parasite on the altars of state—Your Majesty especially must not fail to perceive this.
translations.idiomatic: But Pu submitted another memorial exposing the corruption of Liangsi, Yingzhen, Yanshi, and Yijia, and the circumstances in which Zongwen and Tingyuan shielded Han Jing and Xingbang fawned on Zhao Huan, saying furthermore: "Shijiao is chieftain of the band of villains and is in truth a great parasite on the altars of state—Your Majesty especially must not fail to see this.

sentences.zh: 帝為下詔切責言官，略如樸指。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon issued an edict sharply rebuking the remonstrating officials, largely along the lines Pu had indicated.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then issued an edict sharply rebuking the remonstrating officials, largely along the lines Pu had indicated.

sentences.zh: 黨人益怒，排擊無虛日。

translations.literal: The factionists grew angrier still and attacked without a day of rest.
translations.idiomatic: The factionists grew angrier still and attacked without respite.

sentences.zh: 侍郎李汝華亦以屬吏出位妄言劾樸。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Li Ruhua also impeached Pu on the grounds that a subordinate official had spoken out of turn with reckless words.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Li Ruhua also impeached Pu, claiming that a subordinate had spoken out of turn with reckless words.

sentences.zh: 部院議鐫樸三級，調外任，帝持不下。

translations.literal: The ministries and courts recommended demoting Pu by three ranks and transferring him to an outside post, but the emperor withheld approval.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries and courts recommended demoting Pu by three ranks and transferring him to an outside post, but the emperor withheld approval.

sentences.zh: 至明年四月，吏部奉詔起廢，樸名預焉。

translations.literal: By the fourth month of the following year, the Ministry of Personnel, carrying out an edict to recall dismissed officials, included Pu's name among them.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourth month of the following year, when the Ministry of Personnel carried out an edict recalling dismissed officials, Pu's name was included.

sentences.zh: 於是黨人益嘩，再起攻樸，並及文選郎郭存謙。

translations.literal: Thereupon the factionists grew noisier still, again attacking Pu and extending their attack to Guo Cunqian, secretary in the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: The factionists grew noisier still, again attacking Pu and extending their attack to Guo Cunqian, secretary in the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 存謙引罪，攻者猶未已。

translations.literal: Cunqian acknowledged guilt, but the attackers still did not stop.
translations.idiomatic: Cunqian acknowledged guilt, but the attackers still did not stop.

sentences.zh: 樸益憤，復陳浙人空國之由，追咎沈一貫，詆宗文及毛一鷺甚力，以兩人皆浙產也。

translations.literal: Pu grew angrier still, again stating the reasons Zhejiang men had emptied the state, tracing blame to Shen Yiguan and attacking Zongwen and Mao Yilu with great force, because both were products of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Pu grew angrier still. He again explained how men from Zhejiang had hollowed out the state, traced the blame to Shen Yiguan, and attacked Zongwen and Mao Yilu fiercely—both natives of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 頃之，又再疏劾宗文、一鷺及其黨董定策等。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, he again submitted a memorial impeaching Zongwen, Yilu, and their follower Dong Dingce and others.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, he submitted another memorial impeaching Zongwen, Yilu, and their follower Dong Dingce and others.

sentences.zh: 帝皆置不問。

translations.literal: The emperor put all of it aside without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored it all.

sentences.zh: 其年六月，始用閣臣言，下部院疏，謫樸州同知。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of that year, the court at last followed the grand secretaries' advice, sent down a memorial to the ministries and courts, and demoted Pu to prefectural vice-director.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of that year, the court at last heeded the grand secretaries and sent down a memorial to the ministries and courts demoting Pu to prefectural vice-director.

sentences.zh: 自後黨人益用事，遂以京察落其職。

translations.literal: Afterward the factionists wielded power ever more, and through the capital evaluation they removed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the factionists wielded ever greater power and removed him from office through the capital evaluation.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，起用，歷官參議。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi he was recalled to service and rose to the post of assistant administrator.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign he was recalled to service and rose to assistant administrator.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太僕少卿。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously granted the title of vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢竊柄，御史安伸追論，詔奪其贈。

translations.literal: When Wei Zhongxian usurped power, Censor An Shen pursued the matter in review, and an edict revoked the posthumous grant.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Zhongxian seized power, Censor An Shen pursued the matter, and an edict revoked the posthumous honor.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，復焉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen it was restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign it was restored.

sentences.zh: 夏嘉遇，字正甫，松江華亭人。

translations.literal: Xia Jiayu, styled Zhengfu, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Jiayu, styled Zhengfu, was from Huating in Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十八年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-eighth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-eighth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授保定推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate's aide in Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate's aide in Baoding.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，用治行征。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year he was summoned on account of his record in governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year he was summoned to the capital on account of his record in governance.

sentences.zh: 當擢諫職，先註禮部主事。

translations.literal: He should have been promoted to a remonstrance post, but was first registered as chief clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He should have been promoted to a remonstrance post but was instead registered first as chief clerk in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 帝久倦勤，方從哲獨柄國。

translations.literal: The emperor had long grown weary of diligence; Fang Congzhe alone held the reins of state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long grown weary of governing; Fang Congzhe alone held the reins of state.

sentences.zh: 碌碌充位，中外章奏悉留中。

translations.literal: He filled his seat in mediocrity, and memorials from within and without were all held within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He filled his seat in mediocrity while memorials from within and without the court were all held within the palace.

sentences.zh: 惟言路一攻，則其人自去，不待詔旨。

translations.literal: Yet once the remonstrance channel launched an attack, the target would leave of his own accord without waiting for an edict.
translations.idiomatic: Yet once the remonstrance channel attacked someone, that person would leave of his own accord without waiting for an edict.

sentences.zh: 臺諫之勢，積重不返，有齊、楚、浙三方鼎峙之名。

translations.literal: The power of the censorate remonstrators had accumulated until it could not be reversed, earning the name of the three powers of Qi, Chu, and Zhe standing like a tripod.
translations.idiomatic: The power of the censorate remonstrators had accumulated until it could not be reversed; they were known as the three regional blocs of Qi, Chu, and Zhe, standing in tripartite rivalry.

sentences.zh: 齊則給事中亓詩教、周永春，御史韓浚。

translations.literal: Qi was represented by Supervising Secretaries Qi Shijiao and Zhou Yongchun and Censor Han Jun.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi bloc was led by supervising secretaries Qi Shijiao and Zhou Yongchun and censor Han Jun.

sentences.zh: 楚則給事中官應震、吳亮嗣。

translations.literal: Chu by Supervising Secretaries Guan Yingzhen and Wu Liangsi.
translations.idiomatic: The Chu bloc by supervising secretaries Guan Yingzhen and Wu Liangsi.

sentences.zh: 浙則給事中姚宗文、御史劉廷元。

translations.literal: Zhe by Supervising Secretary Yao Zongwen and Censor Liu Tingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhe bloc by supervising secretary Yao Zongwen and censor Liu Tingyuan.

sentences.zh: 而湯賓尹輩陰為之主。

translations.literal: Tang Binyin and his kind were secretly their masters.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Binyin and his kind were secretly their masters behind the scenes.

sentences.zh: 其黨給事中趙興邦、張延登、徐紹吉、商周祚，御史駱骎曾、過庭訓、房壯麗、牟誌夔、唐世濟、金汝諧、彭宗孟、田生金、李徵儀、董元儒、李嵩輩，與相倡和，務以攻東林排異己為事。

translations.literal: Their faction included Supervising Secretaries Zhao Xingbang, Zhang Yandeng, Xu Shaoji, and Shang Zhouzuo, and Censors Luo Qinzeng, Guo Tingxun, Fang Zhuangli, Mou Zhikui, Tang Shiji, Jin Ruixie, Peng Zongmeng, Tian Shengjin, Li Zhengyi, Dong Yuanru, and Li Song, and the like—they echoed one another, making it their business to attack the Donglin and drive out those unlike themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Their faction included supervising secretaries Zhao Xingbang, Zhang Yandeng, Xu Shaoji, and Shang Zhouzuo, and censors Luo Qinzeng, Guo Tingxun, Fang Zhuangli, Mou Zhikui, Tang Shiji, Jin Ruixie, Peng Zongmeng, Tian Shengjin, Li Zhengyi, Dong Yuanru, Li Song, and others. They echoed one another, devoting themselves to attacking the Donglin and driving out dissenters.

sentences.zh: 其時考選久稽，屢趣不下，言路無幾人，盤踞益堅。

translations.literal: At that time examination and selection were long delayed; though repeatedly urged, nothing was issued. There were few on the remonstrance channel, and their grip grew ever firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Examination and selection were long delayed; though repeatedly urged, nothing was issued. With few remonstrators in place, their grip on power grew ever firmer.

sentences.zh: 後進當入為臺諫者，必鉤致門下，以為羽翼，當事大臣莫敢攖其鋒。

translations.literal: Those junior men who were to enter the censorate remonstrance posts had to be hooked and brought under their wing as supporting wings; no leading minister dared touch their edge.
translations.idiomatic: Junior officials slated for censorate posts had to be recruited into their fold as allies; no leading minister dared challenge them.

sentences.zh: 詩教者，從哲門生，而吏部尚書趙煥鄉人也。

translations.literal: Shijiao was a pupil of Congzhe, and Minister of Personnel Zhao Huan was a fellow townsman.
translations.idiomatic: Shijiao was a pupil of Congzhe, and Minister of Personnel Zhao Huan was his fellow townsman.

sentences.zh: 煥耄昏，兩人一聽詩教。

translations.literal: Huan was senile and confused; the two of them left everything to Shijiao.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was senile and confused; the two of them left everything to Shijiao.

sentences.zh: 詩教把持朝局，為諸黨人魁。

translations.literal: Shijiao controlled the court and was chieftain of all the factionists.
translations.idiomatic: Shijiao controlled the court and was chieftain of the factionists.

sentences.zh: 武進鄒之麟者，浙人黨也。

translations.literal: Zou Zhilin of Wujin was of the Zhejiang faction.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Zhilin of Wujin belonged to the Zhejiang faction.

sentences.zh: 先坐事謫上林典簿，至是為工部主事，附詩教、浚。

translations.literal: He had earlier been demoted to clerk in the Upper Forest Office for an offense; by this time he was chief clerk in the Ministry of Works, attaching himself to Shijiao and Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier been demoted to clerk in the Upper Forest Office for an offense; by this time he was chief clerk in the Ministry of Works and had attached himself to Shijiao and Jun.

sentences.zh: 求吏部不得，大恨，反攻之，並詆從哲。

translations.literal: He sought appointment through the Ministry of Personnel but did not get it, and hated this deeply; he turned to attack them and also slandered Congzhe.
translations.idiomatic: When he failed to obtain appointment through the Ministry of Personnel, he hated this deeply, turned to attack them, and also slandered Congzhe.

sentences.zh: 詩教怒，煥為黜之麟。

translations.literal: Shijiao was angry, and Huan dismissed Zhilin on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Shijiao was furious, and Huan dismissed Zhilin for him.

sentences.zh: 時嘉遇及工部主事鐘惺、中書舍人尹嘉賓、行人魏光國皆以才名，當列言職。

translations.literal: At that time Jiayu, along with Chief Clerk Zhong Xing in the Ministry of Works, Secretariat Drafter Yin Jiabin, and Courier Wei Guangguo, were all famed for talent and should have been appointed to remonstrance posts.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Jiayu, chief clerk Zhong Xing in the Ministry of Works, secretariat drafter Yin Jiabin, and courier Wei Guangguo were all famed for talent and should have been appointed to remonstrance posts.

sentences.zh: 詩教輩以與之麟善，抑之，俾不與考選。

translations.literal: Shijiao and his group, because they were on good terms with Zhilin, suppressed them and kept them from examination and selection.
translations.idiomatic: Shijiao and his group, allied with Zhilin, suppressed them and barred them from examination and selection.

sentences.zh: 以故嘉遇不能無怨。

translations.literal: For this reason Jiayu could not but harbor resentment.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason Jiayu could not but resent it.

sentences.zh: 四十七年三月，遼東敗書聞，嘉遇遂抗疏言：「遼左三路喪師，雖緣楊鎬失策，揆厥所由，則以縱貸李維翰故。

translations.literal: In the third month of the forty-seventh year, when news arrived of the defeat in Liaodong, Jiayu submitted a bold memorial saying: "The loss of armies on the three routes in eastern Liaodong, though caused by Yang Hao's faulty strategy, traced to its root was due to leniency toward Li Weihan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the forty-seventh year, when news arrived of the defeat in Liaodong, Jiayu submitted a bold memorial saying: "The loss of armies on the three routes in eastern Liaodong, though caused by Yang Hao's faulty strategy, traced to its root to leniency toward Li Weihan.

sentences.zh: 夫維翰喪師辱國，罪不容誅，乃僅令回籍聽勘。

translations.literal: Weihan lost armies and shamed the state—a crime that brooked no pardon—yet he was merely ordered to return to his native place pending investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Weihan lost armies and shamed the state—a crime deserving death—yet he was merely ordered to return home pending investigation.

sentences.zh: 誰司票擬？

translations.literal: Who drafted the rescript?
translations.idiomatic: Who drafted the rescript?

sentences.zh: 則閣臣方從哲也；

translations.literal: It was Grand Secretary Fang Congzhe;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Fang Congzhe;

sentences.zh: 誰司糾駁？

translations.literal: Who was charged with review and refutation?
translations.idiomatic: Who was charged with review and censure?

sentences.zh: 則兵科趙興邦也。

translations.literal: It was Zhao Xingbang of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xingbang of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 參貂白鏹，賂遺繹絡，國典邊防，因之大壞。

translations.literal: Sable fur and white silver—bribes flowed in unbroken streams; the laws of the state and frontier defense were thereby greatly ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Sable and silver—bribes flowed in an unbroken stream; the laws of the state and frontier defense were thereby ruined.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下立斷。」

translations.literal: Only Your Majesty's immediate judgment is needed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty must act decisively.

sentences.zh: 疏入，未報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but received no response.

sentences.zh: 從哲力辨，嘉遇再疏劾之，並及詩教。

translations.literal: Congzhe argued forcefully in his defense; Jiayu submitted another memorial impeaching him and also implicating Shijiao.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhe argued forcefully in his defense; Jiayu submitted another memorial impeaching him and also implicating Shijiao.

sentences.zh: 於是詩教、興邦及亮嗣、延登、壯麗輩交章力攻。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shijiao, Xingbang, Liangsi, Yandeng, Zhuangli, and their kind submitted memorial after memorial attacking with full force.
translations.idiomatic: Shijiao, Xingbang, Liangsi, Yandeng, Zhuangli, and their allies then submitted memorial after memorial attacking with full force.

sentences.zh: 詩教謂嘉遇不得考選，故挾私狂逞。

translations.literal: Shijiao said Jiayu, having failed to gain examination and selection, therefore indulged private grievances in reckless outrage.
translations.idiomatic: Shijiao claimed that Jiayu, denied appointment through examination and selection, was venting private grievances in reckless outrage.

sentences.zh: 嘉遇言：「詩教於從哲，一心擁戴，相倚為奸。

translations.literal: Jiayu said: "Shijiao toward Congzhe gives wholehearted support; they rely on each other in wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayu said: "Shijiao gives Congzhe his wholehearted support; they rely on each other in wickedness.

sentences.zh: 凡枚卜、考選諸大政，百方撓阻，專務壅蔽，遏絕主聰。

translations.literal: In all great affairs such as selecting grand secretaries and conducting examinations and appointments, they obstruct by every means, devoting themselves solely to blocking and concealing, cutting off the sovereign's access to knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: On every major matter—selecting grand secretaries, conducting examinations and appointments—they obstruct by every means, devoting themselves to concealment and cutting off the sovereign's access to truth.

sentences.zh: 遂致綱紀不張，戎馬馳突，臣竊痛之。

translations.literal: Thus discipline is not upheld and war-horses charge unchecked—I privately grieve at this.
translations.idiomatic: Thus discipline collapsed and war-horses charged unchecked—I grieve at this from the bottom of my heart.

sentences.zh: 今內治盡壞，縱日議兵食、談戰守，究何益於事？

translations.literal: Now internal governance is utterly ruined; even if day after day one discusses soldiers and provisions and talks of war and defense, what benefit can it ultimately bring to affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Internal governance is utterly ruined; even if day after day we discuss troops and provisions and debate strategy, what good can it ultimately do?

sentences.zh: 故臣為國擊奸，冀除禍本，雖死不避，尚區區計升沈得喪哉！」

translations.literal: Therefore your subject strikes at villains for the sake of the state, hoping to remove the root of calamity; though death I do not avoid—would I still fuss over petty rises and falls, gains and losses!"
translations.idiomatic: I strike at villains for the sake of the state, hoping to uproot the source of calamity. I do not shrink from death—why would I fuss over petty promotions and demotions!"

sentences.zh: 時興邦以右給事中掌兵科。

translations.literal: At the time Xingbang, as Right Supervising Secretary, supervised the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xingbang, as right supervising secretary, supervised the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 先有旨，俟遼東底寧，從優敘錄。

translations.literal: There had earlier been an edict that when Liaodong was fully pacified, he would be favorably promoted and recorded.
translations.idiomatic: An earlier edict had promised that once Liaodong was pacified, he would be favorably promoted.

sentences.zh: 至是以嘉遇連劾，吏部遂立擢為太常少卿。

translations.literal: At this point, because Jiayu had impeached him repeatedly, the Ministry of Personnel immediately promoted him to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At this point, despite Jiayu's repeated impeachments, the Ministry of Personnel immediately promoted him to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 嘉遇益憤，疏言：「四路奏功，興邦必將預其賞。

translations.literal: Jiayu grew angrier still and submitted a memorial saying: "When the four routes report success, Xingbang will surely share in the reward.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayu grew angrier still and submitted a memorial saying: "When the four routes report success, Xingbang will surely share in the reward.

sentences.zh: 則今日事敗，興邦安得逃其罰？

translations.literal: Then when affairs fail today, how can Xingbang escape punishment?
translations.idiomatic: Then when affairs fail today, how can Xingbang escape blame?

sentences.zh: 且不罰已矣，反從而超陟之。

translations.literal: Not only is he not punished—he is instead promoted beyond his rank.
translations.idiomatic: Not only is he not punished—he is promoted beyond his rank.

sentences.zh: 是臣彈章適為薦剡，國家有如是法紀哉！」

translations.literal: Thus your subject's impeachment memorial has served precisely as a recommendation—does the state have such laws and discipline!
translations.idiomatic: My impeachment has served precisely as a letter of recommendation—does the state have such laws!

sentences.zh: 疏奏，諸御史復合詞攻嘉遇。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the censors again joined in attacking Jiayu with one voice.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the censors again joined in attacking Jiayu.

sentences.zh: 嘉遇復疏言：「古人有雲，見無禮於君者逐之，如鷹鹯之逐鳥雀也。

translations.literal: Jiayu submitted another memorial saying: "The ancients said that when one sees a man behave without propriety toward the ruler, one drives him away as a hawk or eagle drives small birds.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayu submitted another memorial saying: "The ancients said that when one sees a man behave without propriety toward the ruler, one drives him away as a hawk drives small birds.

sentences.zh: 詩教、興邦謂臣不得臺諫而怒。

translations.literal: Shijiao and Xingbang say your subject is angry because he did not obtain a censorate remonstrance post.
translations.idiomatic: Shijiao and Xingbang claim I am angry because I failed to obtain a censorate post.

sentences.zh: 夫爵位名秩，操之天子，人臣何敢幹？

translations.literal: Ranks and titles are controlled by the Son of Heaven—how dare a subject interfere?
translations.idiomatic: Ranks and titles belong to the Son of Heaven—how dare a subject interfere?

sentences.zh: 必如所言，是考選予奪，二臣實專之。

translations.literal: If what they say were true, then in granting and withholding examination and selection these two ministers actually monopolize the power.
translations.idiomatic: If what they say were true, then these two ministers in fact monopolize the granting and withholding of appointments.

sentences.zh: 此無禮於君者一。

translations.literal: This is the first instance of impropriety toward the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: This is the first act of impropriety toward the ruler.

sentences.zh: 事寧優敘，非明旨乎？

translations.literal: Favorable promotion once affairs are settled—is that not a clear edict?
translations.idiomatic: Favorable promotion once affairs are settled—was that not a clear edict?

sentences.zh: 乃竟蔑而棄之。

translations.literal: Yet they actually despised and cast it aside.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they despised it and cast it aside.

sentences.zh: 此無禮於君者二。

translations.literal: This is the second instance of impropriety toward the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: This is the second act of impropriety toward the ruler.

sentences.zh: 魏光國疏論詩教，為通政沮格。

translations.literal: Wei Guangguo submitted a memorial discussing Shijiao, but it was obstructed and blocked by the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Guangguo submitted a memorial discussing Shijiao, but the Office of Transmission obstructed and blocked it.

sentences.zh: 夫要截實封者斬。

translations.literal: To intercept sealed memorials merits execution.
translations.idiomatic: Intercepting sealed memorials is punishable by death.

sentences.zh: 自來奸臣不敢為，而詩教為之。

translations.literal: Never before have evil ministers dared do this, yet Shijiao has done it.
translations.idiomatic: Evil ministers had never dared do this—yet Shijiao did.

sentences.zh: 此無禮於君者三。

translations.literal: This is the third instance of impropriety toward the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: This is the third act of impropriety toward the ruler.

sentences.zh: 二奸每事請托，一日以七事屬職方郎楊成喬。

translations.literal: The two villains entrust affairs on every occasion; one day they entrusted seven matters to Yang Chengqiao, secretary in the Bureau of Military Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: The two villains routinely traded in favors; one day they entrusted seven matters to Yang Chengqiao, secretary in the Bureau of Military Appointments.

sentences.zh: 成喬不聽，遂逐之去。

translations.literal: Chengqiao would not listen, and so they drove him away.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqiao refused, and they drove him out.

sentences.zh: 詩教以舊憾欲去其鄉知府，考功郎陳顯道不從，亦逼之去。

translations.literal: Shijiao, because of an old grudge, wished to remove the prefect of his native district; Chen Xiandao, secretary in the Bureau of Evaluations, would not comply, and they also forced him out.
translations.idiomatic: Shijiao, nursing an old grudge, sought to remove the prefect of his native district; Chen Xiandao, secretary in the Bureau of Evaluations, refused, and they forced him out as well.

sentences.zh: 夫吏、兵二部，天子所以馭天下也，而二奸敢侵越之。

translations.literal: The two ministries of Personnel and War are how the Son of Heaven governs the realm—yet the two villains dare to encroach upon them.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries of Personnel and War are how the Son of Heaven governs the realm—yet these two villains dare to encroach upon them.

sentences.zh: 此無禮於君者四。

translations.literal: These are four instances of disrespect toward the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: These are four ways he has shown disrespect toward the ruler.

sentences.zh: 有臣如此，臣義豈與俱生哉！」

translations.literal: With ministers such as these, how could a minister in duty consent to live together with them!"
translations.idiomatic: With ministers such as these, how could I in conscience go on living among them!"

sentences.zh: 先是，三黨諸魁交甚密，後齊與浙漸相貳。

translations.literal: Earlier the chiefs of the three factions were on very intimate terms; later the Qi and Zhe factions gradually grew estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the chiefs of the three factions had been very close; later the Qi and Zhe factions gradually grew estranged.

sentences.zh: 布衣汪文言者，素遊黃正賓、於玉立之門，習知黨人本末。

translations.literal: The commoner Wang Wenyan had long frequented the circles of Huang Zhengbin and Yu Yuli and was well versed in the origins and ends of the factionalists.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner named Wang Wenyan had long moved in the circles of Huang Zhengbin and Yu Yuli and knew the factionalists' history inside out.

sentences.zh: 後玉立遣之入都，益悉諸黨人所為，策之曰：「浙人者，主兵也，齊、楚則應兵。

translations.literal: Later Yuli sent him to the capital, where he came to know still more fully what the factionalists were doing, and laid a plan, saying: The Zhe men are the ones who command the troops; Qi and Chu respond to the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yuli sent him to the capital, where he learned still more of what the factionalists were doing and laid a plan: 'The Zhe men command the troops; Qi and Chu answer to them.

sentences.zh: 成功之後，主欲逐客矣，然柄素在客，未易逐，此可構也。」

translations.literal: After success the master will wish to drive out the guests, yet power has long lain with the guests and they are not easily driven out—this can be engineered.
translations.idiomatic: After success the master will wish to drive out the guests, yet power has long lain with the guests and they are not easily expelled—this can be engineered.

sentences.zh: 遂多方設奇間之，諸人果相疑。

translations.literal: Thereupon he set up stratagems on many sides to sow discord among them, and the men indeed grew suspicious of one another.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he devised stratagems on many sides to sow discord among them, and they indeed grew suspicious of one another.

sentences.zh: 而鄒之麟既見惡齊黨，亦交鬥其間。

translations.literal: Zou Zhilin, already hated by the Qi faction, also joined in the mutual strife.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Zhilin, already hated by the Qi faction, also joined in the mutual strife.

sentences.zh: 揚言齊人張鳳翔為文選，必以年例斥宗文、廷元。

translations.literal: It was rumored that Zhang Fengxiang of the Qi faction, once in charge of the Selection Office, would by annual rule dismiss Zongwen and Tingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor had it that Zhang Fengxiang of the Qi faction, once in charge of the Selection Office, would use the annual rule to dismiss Zongwen and Tingyuan.

sentences.zh: 於是齊、浙之黨大離。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Qi and Zhe factions split sharply apart.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Qi and Zhe factions split sharply apart.

sentences.zh: 及是嘉遇五疏力攻，詩教輩亦窘。

translations.literal: At this point Jiayu attacked forcefully in five memorials, and Shijiao and his group were also hard pressed.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Jiayu attacked forcefully in five memorials, and Shijiao and his group were also hard pressed.

sentences.zh: 而浙人唐世濟、董元儒遂助嘉遇排擊。

translations.literal: The Zhe men Tang Shiji and Dong Yuanru then aided Jiayu in pressing the attack.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhe men Tang Shiji and Dong Yuanru then aided Jiayu in pressing the attack.

sentences.zh: 自是亓、趙之勢頓衰，興邦竟不果遷，自引去。

translations.literal: From this the power of Qi and Zhao suddenly declined; Xingbang in the end did not obtain transfer and withdrew on his own.
translations.idiomatic: From this the power of the Qi and Zhao factions suddenly declined; Xingbang in the end did not obtain transfer and withdrew on his own.

sentences.zh: 時論快焉。

translations.literal: Public opinion rejoiced at it.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，嘉遇乞改南部，就遷吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangzong ascended the throne, Jiayu asked to transfer to the southern capital and was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangzong ascended the throne, Jiayu asked to transfer to the southern capital and was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，趙南星秉銓，召為考功員外郎，改文選署選事。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign Zhao Nanxing held the power of appointment and summoned him as Vice Director of the Bureau of Evaluations, then transferred him to the Selection Office to handle appointments.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianqi reign Zhao Nanxing held the power of appointment and summoned him as Vice Director of the Bureau of Evaluations, then transferred him to the Selection Office to handle appointments.

sentences.zh: 時左光鬥、魏大中以嘉遇與之麟、韓敬同年相善，頗疑之。

translations.literal: At that time Zuo Guangdou and Wei Zhongxian, knowing Jiayu was on friendly terms with his fellow jinshi Zhilin and Han Jing, were rather suspicious of him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zuo Guangdou and Wei Zhongxian, knowing Jiayu was on friendly terms with his fellow jinshi Zhilin and Han Jing, were rather suspicious of him.

sentences.zh: 已，見嘉遇公廉，亦皆親善。

translations.literal: Later, seeing Jiayu's public integrity, they all drew close to him as well.
translations.idiomatic: Later, seeing Jiayu's public integrity, they all drew close to him as well.

sentences.zh: 及陳九疇劾謝應祥，語連嘉遇，鐫三級，調外，語具南星傳。

translations.literal: When Chen Jiuchou impeached Xie Yingxiang, language implicated Jiayu; he was reduced three grades and transferred outside the capital—the details are given in Nanxing's biography.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Jiuchou impeached Xie Yingxiang, language implicated Jiayu; he was reduced three grades and transferred outside the capital—the details are given in Nanxing's biography.

sentences.zh: 未幾，黨人張訥誣劾南星，並及嘉遇，遂除名。

translations.literal: Before long the factionalist Zhang Ne falsely impeached Nanxing and implicated Jiayu as well; he was struck from the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the factionalist Zhang Ne falsely impeached Nanxing and implicated Jiayu as well; he was struck from the registers.

sentences.zh: 尋鍛煉光鬥、大中獄，誣嘉遇嘗行賄。

translations.literal: Soon, in forging the cases against Guangdou and Dazhong in prison, they falsely charged that Jiayu had once given bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, in forging the cases against Guangdou and Dazhong in prison, they falsely charged that Jiayu had once given bribes.

sentences.zh: 逮訊論徒，憤恨發病卒。

translations.literal: When he was arrested, interrogated, and sentenced to penal servitude, he died of illness brought on by indignation.
translations.idiomatic: When he was arrested, interrogated, and sentenced to penal servitude, he died of illness brought on by indignation.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，贈太常少卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign he was posthumously granted Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign he was posthumously granted Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：李植、江東之諸人，風節自許，矯首抗俗，意氣橫厲，抵排群枉，跡不違乎正。

translations.literal: The eulogist says: Li Zhi, Jiang Dongzhi, and the others prided themselves on integrity and moral bearing, held their heads high against the vulgar world, were fierce and overbearing in spirit, struck down the wicked in groups, and in their conduct did not depart from the right.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogist says: Li Zhi, Jiang Dongzhi, and their fellows prided themselves on integrity and moral bearing, held their heads high against the vulgar world, were fierce and overbearing in spirit, struck down the wicked in groups, and in their conduct did not depart from the right.

sentences.zh: 而質之矜而不爭、群而不黨之義，不能無疚心焉。

translations.literal: Yet measured against the principle of being proud yet not contentious, banding together yet not forming factions, they cannot be without a troubled conscience.
translations.idiomatic: Yet measured against the principle of being proud yet not contentious, banding together yet not forming factions, they cannot be without a troubled conscience.

sentences.zh: 「古之矜也廉，今之矜也忿戾」，聖人所為致慨於末世之益衰也。

translations.literal: "In antiquity pride meant integrity; today pride means resentment and violence"—it is for this that the sage lamented the ever greater decline of the late age.
translations.idiomatic: "In antiquity pride meant integrity; today pride means resentment and violence"—it is for this that the sage lamented the ever greater decline of the late age.
